instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 177.42 Definitions (prevailing wage on state-funded projects, sections 177.41 to 177.44)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Definitions for 177.41-177.44. "Project" = demolition, erection, construction, alteration, improvement, restoration, remodeling or repair of a public building, structure, facility, land or other public work financed in whole or part by state funds (also when acquisition, predesign, design or demolition is state-financed). "Prevailing hours of labor" cannot exceed 8 per day or 40 per week. "Prevailing wage rate" = hourly basic rate plus contributions for medical, pensions, injury compensation, unemployment, life/disability insurance, vacation and holiday pay, apprenticeship and other bona fide fringe benefits; cannot be less than a reasonable and living wage; includes truck-hire rental rates for 177.44. Establishes that a Minnesota state prevailing-wage regime exists (public projects only). Rates and thresholds are not in this section.

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-371 Earned paid sick time - definitions
figure_or_rule_carried: Earned paid sick time is paid at the same hourly rate and with the same benefits the employee normally earns, never below the FLSA or state minimum wage (D). Employer covers private entities and political subdivisions, but not the State of Arizona or the United States (G). Year = regular consecutive 12-month period chosen by the employer (L).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-372 Accrual of earned paid sick time
figure_or_rule_carried: Accrual 1 hour per 30 hours worked. Annual accrual/use cap 40 hours (15+ employees) or 24 hours (<15 employees) unless the employer sets higher (A, B). Headcount counts full-time, part-time and temporary; 15+ on payroll in 20 calendar weeks of the current or preceding year (C). Accrual from hire; 90-day use wait allowed (D1-2). FLSA-exempt employees assumed to work 40 h/week (D3). Carry-over required, or pay unused time at year end and front-load (D4). Rehire within 9 months reinstates the balance (D5); successor employer carries balances (D6). An equivalent PTO policy satisfies the article (E). No payout of unused time on separation required (F).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-373 Use of earned paid sick time
figure_or_rule_carried: Uses: own or family illness, care and preventive care; public-health closure of the workplace or of a child's school/care; domestic violence, sexual violence, abuse or stalking (A). Smallest increment = the smaller of one hour or the smallest increment the payroll system uses for absences (F). Documentation only for 3+ consecutive work days (G).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-377 Confidentiality of earned paid sick time information (with 23-374)

figure_or_rule_carried: Wages due for regular pay periods no longer than one calendar month or 30 days (whichever longer), paid on regular paydays no later than 10 days after the close of the period, unless employer and employee agree otherwise (8-4-103(1)(a)). Direct deposit only if the employee voluntarily authorised deposit in the institution of the employee's choice (8-4-102(2)). Paycard allowed only if the employee has free access to the entire net pay at least once per pay period, or may choose another payment means (8-4-102(2.5)). Checks must be negotiable without discount (8-4-102(1)). Paydays must be posted (8-4-107).

instrument_name: Colorado Wage Act C.R.S. 8-4-109(1) final pay; 8-4-101(14)(a)(III) vacation pay; 8-4-101(14)(b) severance
authority: Colorado General Assembly (text published by CDLE)
figure_or_rule_carried: Discharge (employer volition): wages earned, vested, determinable and unpaid due immediately; if payroll unit not operational, available within 6 hours of the start of its next regular workday, or within 24 hours if the unit is off-site (delivered to work site, local office or last mailing address). Resignation: due on the next regular payday. Unclaimed check mailed after 60 days. Vacation: employer that provides paid vacation must pay on separation all vacation earned and determinable under the agreement (wages, 8-4-101(14)(a)(III)). Severance is not wages (14)(b). Penalty after written demand unpaid 14 days: greater of 2x unpaid wages or 1,000 USD (8-4-109(3)(b)).

instrument_name: Colorado Wage Act C.R.S. 8-4-105 permitted payroll deductions
authority: Colorado General Assembly (text published by CDLE)
figure_or_rule_carried: Only these deductions: (a) required by law (taxes, FICA, garnishments, court orders); (a.5) automatic enrolment retirement contributions; (b) loans, advances, goods/services, equipment under a written enforceable agreement; (c) theft shortage after a police report (refund with interest if no charge within 90 days or acquittal); (d) other deductions authorised by the employee if the authorisation is revocable (insurance, savings, stock, charities, deposits); (e) unreturned money/property of a terminated employee entrusted with it, with notice within 10 calendar days of termination.

instrument_name: Colorado Judicial Branch Form 26 SC, Writ of Continuing Garnishment (R: 1/22), incl. Calculation of the Amount of Exempt Earnings and Explanation of Wage Garnishment
article_or_section: Notice to Garnishee a-f; Calculation; Exemption Chart; Explanation (implements C.R.S. 13-54-104 and 13-54.5)
figure_or_rule_carried: Disposable earnings = gross less deductions required by law (income taxes, FICA) AND employer-provided health insurance withheld (CO departure from CCPA). Amount exempt = greater of 80% of disposable earnings or 40x (weekly) / 80x (bi-weekly) / 86.67x (semi-monthly) / 173.3x (monthly) the minimum hourly wage, where minimum hourly wage = state or federal, whichever greater; i.e. garnish the lesser of 20% of disposable earnings or the excess over 40x minimum wage (weekly). Wage/income assignments (support) in the period are deducted first; a writ for support or prior continuing writ takes priority and the new writ starts after it terminates. Garnishee pays from the first pay date at least 21 days after service. Tips excluded from 'earnings' on this form. 2026 weekly floor derived: 40 x 15.16 = 606.40 USD. Statute text 13-54-104 itself not read on an official host (CRS official host is LexisNexis, gated).

instrument_name: 19 Del. C. ch. 9 Minimum Wage Act (901-914)
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage 15.00/h effective 2025-01-01 (902(a)(5)); last statutory step, no indexation and no 2027 step in the text; becomes the federal rate if federal exceeds it. Tipped: tip credit = federal tip-credit percentage as of 2006-06-15 of the state minimum, cash wage never below 2.23/h (902(b)); tipped occupation = customarily >30/month in tips (902(c)(1)); tips are the employee's property, employer-mandated pool max 15% of primary direct-service employee's tips (902(d)(2)). Excluded from 'employee' (901(3)): agriculture, domestic service in a private home, bona fide EAP and outside sales, US government employees, gratuitous nonprofit volunteers, fishing/first processing at sea, under-18 summer camp counselors, DOC inmates (unless private employer), minor-league baseball under CBA. Records 3 years: name, address, occupation, rate, amount paid each period, hours each day and week (907).

instrument_name: 19 Del. C. ch. 11 Wage Payment and Collection Act (1101-1115)
figure_or_rule_carried: Coverage: private employers; excludes US, State of Delaware and political subdivisions (1101(4)-(5)). Pay at least once per calendar month on paydays designated in advance; within 7 days of the close of the pay period; nonwork payday -> preceding workday; overtime/new hires/variable part-timers may slip to next period if pay period <= 16 days and payday within period (1102(a)-(b)). Direct deposit only on the employee's written request (1102(a)). Final pay: on quit, discharge, suspension or layoff wages due on the LATER of the next regular payday or 3 business days after the last day worked, usual channel or by mail on request (1103(a)); liquidated damages lower of 10%/day or the unpaid wages (1103(b)(2)). Deductions only if required by law, for medical care without employer benefit, or with signed employee authorization for a lawful purpose for the employee's benefit (1107). Employers of over 3 employees: written notice at hire of rate and day/hour/place of payment; pay statement at time of payment on the check, a separate slip or electronically if retainable, showing wages due, pay period, total deductions separately specified, and hours for hourly employees; employee may request paper; records 3 years (1108). Benefits/wage supplements (incl. vacation, separation pay) payable within 30 days after due under the agreement (1109). Wage theft 1102A: failure to withhold taxes or forward withholding within 7 days of the pay period is a violation, civil penalty 2,000-20,000 per violation.

figure_or_rule_carried: Nonresident tax = resident-basis tax under 1102 less 1110(b) credit, times modified DE-source income / DE AGI (1121). Employee compensation is DE-source if for services (a) rendered in DE or (b) attributable to employment in DE and not required to be performed elsewhere (1124(b)(1)) - the statutory basis of Delaware's convenience-of-the-employer rule (employer-necessity test). instrument_name: 30 Del. C. 1151-1156A Withholding, W-2, returns, deposit frequency, new hires
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer with an office or business in DE withholds from resident or nonresident wages taxable under ch. 11 when the wages are subject to federal withholding; method/tables prescribed by the Division (1151(a)); employee has the same number of exemptions as for federal purposes, employer may rely on the federal count (1151(b)); reciprocity agreements authorised but none in force (1151(c); FAQ US-DEWH-001). W-2 to employee by Jan 31, or within 30 days of last wage payment on termination (1152). Filing frequency by July-June lookback: quarterly <= 4,500, monthly 4,500-25,000 (or no DE employees in lookback), eighth-monthly > 25,000, thresholds indexed under 30 Del. C. 515 (1154(a)); quarterly due last day of month after quarter; monthly by the 15th of next month; eighth-monthly 3 working days after periods ending 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, 19th, 22nd, 25th, last day (1154(c)-(e)); EFT if federal EFT required, with 1-year lag (1154(g)); W-2/1099 information returns to the Division by Jan 31, in machine-readable form when required federally (1154(i)). New hires to the State Directory of New Hires within 20 days (or 2 monthly electronic transmissions 12-16 days apart; multistate employer may designate one state): name, address, SSN, first day of paid service, employer name, address, FEIN, on W-4 or equivalent; rehire after 60+ days separation counts; fine 25 per failure, 500 for conspiracy (1156A). 1154 last amended by 85 Del. figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base: 12,500 for 2025; 14,500 from 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31; 16,500 after 2026-12-31 (or the FUTA base if higher) (3302(28)(A)(vii)-(ix)); the older trust-fund-tiered 18,500/16,500/14,500 rule in (vi) is displaced for these years by the dated paragraphs (DOL FAQ still prints 18,500 and 10,500: stale). 3302(28)(A)(x): for the wage-base computation 'employment' includes service covered by another state's UI law -> wages paid by the same employer and reported to another state in the year count toward the DE 14,500. instrument_name: 19 Del. C. ch. 37 Healthy Delaware Families Act (Delaware Paid Leave): coverage, contributions, benefits
figure_or_rule_carried: Statutory contribution rates for 2025 AND 2026: medical 0.40%, family caregiving 0.08%, parental 0.32% of wages (3705(b)(1)-(3)); from 2027 set annually by the Department on actuarial principles, total capped at 1.00% (above that, benefit % is cut) (3705(b),(c)). Employer may deduct NOT MORE than 50% of each contribution from the employee, may pay more; deduction only concurrent with and proportionate to wages paid; employer liable for the full amount if not deducted (3705(d)-(g)). Remittance quarterly or as the Department regulates (3705(b)). Waiver form where schedule/tenure won't meet eligibility (3705(k)). Wages = FICA wages (3701(24)) -> capped at the Social Security wage base. Employer coverage (3701(7)): 10-24 employees in previous 12 months = parental leave only (0.32%); 25+ = all three (0.80%); fewer than 10 not covered (voluntary). Employee = primarily reporting for work at a DE worksite; out-of-state worksite employees excluded unless the employer elects (3701(6)a) -> multistate coverage follows the primary worksite, not UI localization. Covered individual: 12 months and 1,250 hours with the employer (3701(3)). Benefits: 80% of average weekly wage, min 100, max 900/week in 2026 and 2027, then CPI-U Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington indexed (3704(a)); 12 weeks parental per application year; 6 weeks medical/caregiving per 24 months (3703). Claimant told benefits may be taxable; taxes withheld per regulation (3714). Supersedes the tier-B levy row US-DEP7-002 for the rate (now statute-backed).

instrument_name: 10 Del. C. 4913 Exemption and attachment of wages
figure_or_rule_carried: 85% of the wages of any person residing in Delaware is exempt from mesne and execution attachment (so creditor garnishment max 15% of wages, vs CCPA 25% of disposable earnings - apply the more protective of the two per pay period); the 85% limit does not apply to process for fines, costs or taxes owed to the State. Only one attachment at a time on any amount of wages due; first attaching creditor has priority until paid in full. Wages include salaries, commissions and every other remuneration for services (not self-employment). Base is 'wages' (gross wording), not 'disposable earnings' - the comparison with CCPA must be done per payment.

instrument_name: 29 Del. C. 6960 Prevailing wage requirements (public works)
figure_or_rule_carried: Applies to State or subdivision public works contracts with State funds over 500,000 (new construction incl. painting/decorating) or 45,000 (alteration, repair, renovation, demolition, reconstruction). Rates set by DOL; CBA rates adopted where they prevailed 4 of last 5 years, raise per CBA as of September 1. Laborers and mechanics paid unconditionally at least WEEKLY, no deductions or rebates beyond lawful ones; sworn payroll information furnished WEEKLY as required by DOL (certified payroll), retained by DOL 6 months; civil penalty 1,000-5,000 per violation incl. failure to submit payroll reports or post the rates; treble damages; not applicable to DOT Community Transportation Fund or Municipal Street Aid projects.

instrument_name: 13 Del. C. 513 Judgment; order of support; income withholding and employer duties
figure_or_rule_carried: Support attachments are not subject to the 10 Del. C. 4913 85% exemption; limited by CCPA 303(b) (15 U.S.C. 1673(b)); priority over every other attachment except federal tax liens, regardless of date (513(b)(7)). Arrears add-on: current support plus up to 20% of current support or 20/month, whichever greater, where no arrears payment ordered or it is below 20% (513(b)(2)b). Employer deducts the specified sum and may deduct a State-established fee unless it waives it (amount NOT stated in the statute); remit at or before payday; start no later than 7 days after the first payday following receipt; remittance shows obligor name and SSN; one combined payment allowed to DCSS; for another state's IWO apply the law of the obligor's principal place of employment for 411(d) factors (513(b)(8)a). Employers with 50+ employees must remit to DCSS by EFT/EDI (513(b)(8)b). Notify court/DCSS of termination with last address and new employer; NMSN to plan within 20 business days. Penalties: up to 1,000 / 90 days first offense for non-compliance or dismissal due to attachment, up to 5,000 thereafter (513(b)(10)); 100-500 fine for not answering a DCSS information request within 30 days (513(f)).

Every new or rehired employee reported within 20 days of hire date (date of hire = first day of work for which income is owed), or by two monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart if electronic; W-4 or equivalent; fields: employee name, address, date of hire, SSN; employer name, address, FEIN; DOB optional. instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 218.077 Wage and employment benefits requirements by political subdivisions (preemption)
figure_or_rule_carried: Counties, municipalities and other political subdivisions may not mandate a minimum wage other than state/federal, nor employment benefits (incl. paid/unpaid sick leave, vacation, holidays) not required by state/federal law, nor control contractor wages through purchasing (ch. 2024-80). Exceptions: their own employees; employers receiving a direct tax abatement/subsidy as a condition. Ch. 2024-80 amendments do not impair contracts entered before 2026-09-30. Result: no local minimum wage or local paid-sick-leave mandate on private employers in Florida.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 450.081 Hours of work of minors
figure_or_rule_carried: Minors 15 and under: not before 7am/after 7pm on school nights, max 15 h/week in school session, 3 h on school days; holidays/summer 7am-9pm, 8 h/day, 40 h/week; max 6 consecutive days; 30-min meal after 4 h. Minors 16-17: not before 6:30am/after 11pm on school nights, 8 h on school-night days, 30 h/week in session (waivable by parent or superintendent); 30-min meal after 4 h when working 8+ h. Exemptions: graduates, certificate holders, hardship, home/virtual education 16-17, domestic service in private homes, children of the employer. No minor sub-minimum wage in state law.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 222.11 Exemption of wages from garnishment

Others: CCPA limit. Exempt earnings stay exempt 6 months in a bank account if traceable. Not indexed.

instrument_name: Fla. Stat. 61.1301 Income deduction orders (child support)
figure_or_rule_carried: Payor may charge the obligor up to $5 for the first deduction and $2 per deduction thereafter (within the CCPA 1673(b) limit incl. charges); implement no later than the first payment date more than 14 days after service; remit within 2 days after each pay date; arrears add 20% or more of the periodic amount; income deduction has priority over all other legal processes under state law; multiple orders prorated with priority to current support; termination notice to obligee/IV-D agency (civil penalty $250 first / $500 subsequent); no discharge for income deduction.

instrument_name: Florida DOR Employer Guide to Reemployment Tax (RT-800002, R. 03/25)
article_or_section: pp.2-3 liability; pp.8-11 RT-6, wage base, annual option, taxable/exempt wages, BLS-3020, RT-6EW, E-Verify
figure_or_rule_carried: Liability: $1,500 wages in a quarter, or 1 employee in 20 weeks, or FUTA liability (current/preceding year); domestic $1,000 in a quarter. RT-6 due by the last day of the month after the quarter (Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31); report required even with no tax due; electronic payment initiated by 5 pm ET the business day before the due date. RT-7 annual domestic report due Jan 1, late after Jan 31. Wage portion: name, SSN, gross and taxable wages per employee; penalty up to $300 for wrong/missing SSN. Wages reported when paid. $7,000 base per employer; successor may count predecessor wages; out-of-state wages credited via RT-6NF. Taxable: commissions (except solely-commissioned real estate/insurance agents and barbers), bonuses, back pay, tips reported under IRC 6053(a), non-cash remuneration, personal-use car, non-convenience meals/lodging, group legal, golden parachutes. Exempt: church/minister, students at their school, co-op students, family employment, cafeteria plan payments not reportable to IRS, IRC 127 education. Multi-worksite employers file BLS-3020 quarterly; contractors to public/nonprofit educational institutions file RT-6EW.

Due last day of month after quarter (next business day if weekend/holiday); electronic filing and payment mandatory for employers with 10+ employees in any quarter of the prior state fiscal year (Jul-Jun). Prior-quarter corrections on RT-8A (online if e-filer). Signed by owner/officer/partner or authorised agent. Form on Rule 73B-10.037 F.A.C. (rule text not read).

instrument_name: GA DOR Employer's Withholding Tax Guide 2026 (rev. September 2026), Percentage Method Tables E/F and worked examples
article_or_section: pp. 51-52 (Tables E, F; Examples 1 and 2); p. 31 ff. Tax Tables A-D
figure_or_rule_carried: Percentage method: (1) wages less standard deduction per period [annual 30,000 MFJ / 15,000 Single-HoH / 15,000 MFS; weekly 576.92/288.46/288.46; biweekly 1,153.85/576.92; semimonthly 1,250.00/625.00; monthly 2,500.00/1,250.00; quarterly 7,500/3,750; semiannual 15,000/7,500; daily 82.19/41.10]; (2) less dependent allowance per dependent [annual 5,000; weekly 96.15; biweekly 192.31; semimonthly 208.33; monthly 416.67; quarterly 1,250; semiannual 2,500; daily 13.70]; (3) x 4.99%. Married couples both earning use MFS column. Example 1 (MFJ semimonthly 2,000, 1 dependent): 2,000-1,250-208.33=541.67 x 0.0499 = 27.03 (re-derived 27.029333). Example 2 (HoH biweekly 935, 2 dependents): 0.00. Tax tables (pp. 31-50) priced at the upper bound of each wage bracket: Single weekly 276-294 -> 0.28 = (294-288.46) x 0.0499 = 0.2764 (re-derived). Guide states tables and percentage method give slightly different results; no rounding instruction (cents).

instrument_name: GA DOR Employer's Withholding Tax Guide 2026: Withholding due dates and Withholding Requirements Summary
figure_or_rule_carried: Payer status by lookback (12 months ending 30 June prior year): semi-weekly if > 50,000 (EFT; Wed/Thu/Fri payday -> following Wednesday; Sat-Tue -> following Friday; G-7 Schedule B quarterly); monthly if > 200/month (GA-V by 15th of following month; G-7 for monthly payer by last day of month after quarter); quarterly if <= 200/month and > 800/year (G-7 by last day of month after quarter); annual if <= 800/year (G-7 by 31 January, request via GTC). One-day rule: > 100,000 withheld for a payday -> EFT next banking day. Any G-7 > 500 -> EFT thereafter and mandatory e-filing; EFT failure penalty 10%. Zero G-7 required while account active. 2026 dates: Q3 G-7 2026-11-02; Q4 G-7 2027-02-01. Registration on GTC (gtc.dor.ga.gov), number and frequency issued within 15 minutes. Final G-7 within 30 days of ceasing to have employees. Late payment penalty 25 + 5%/month, cap 25 + 25%; interest prime + 3%.

instrument_name: GA DOR Employer's Withholding Tax Guide 2026: Income Statement Reporting Requirements (G-1003, W-2, 1099)
figure_or_rule_carried: W-2s and 1099-NEC with GA withholding filed with Form G-1003 by 31 January (TY2026: 2027-02-01); other 1099s by 28 February (2027-03-01); W-2 not required if no GA withholding. Electronic filing mandatory if federally required to e-file, or if paying by EFT (mandatory or voluntary). Formats: GTC manual entry, G-1003 template/CSV, or Federal Format (EFW2) with Georgia-defined RS record (TY2026 specs 'available late October 2026'); 1099 via IRIS XML (FIRE/Pub 1220 no longer accepted from TY2026). GA does not participate in CF/SF for statements with GA withholding. TY2026: qualified overtime (W-2 box 12 TT) and cash tips (box 12 TP, box 14b TTOC) reported on W-2; RLA employees 'GA OT' in box 14a; no separate G-7 fields in 2026; from 2027 G-7 collects quarterly overtime/tip totals and employee counts. Business closing: statements due 30 days after final wages. Late statement penalties 10/20/50 per statement (caps 50k/100k/200k).

instrument_name: GA DOR Employer's Withholding Tax Guide 2026: definitions, G-4, special payments
figure_or_rule_carried: Resident: legal resident, or lives in GA on regular/permanent basis, or 183+ days in 365-day period ending 31 Dec. Taxable nonresident: > 5% of wages or > 5,000 attributable to GA. Residents working in another state: no GA withholding if the other state requires withholding. G-4 (name, address, SSN, filing status, allowances, additional withholding); no G-4 -> use W-4 if sufficient, else Single zero allowances; G-4 claiming exempt or > 14 allowances mailed to DOR; exempt G-4 valid until 15 February following year; new G-4 effective first payroll after receipt. Bonuses: rate in effect when paid (5.19% before 2026-05-11, may use 4.99% from 2026-05-11). Domestic workers (housekeepers, nannies), farm laborers and ministers: withholding not required (voluntary). Severance: withhold if resident when paid; nonresident at payment -> no GA withholding. 401(k)/profit-sharing/deferred comp: GA follows federal, pre-tax. 1099-NEC without valid TIN: 6% for labor in GA. Payroll records retained >= 4 years.

instrument_name: GDOL Employer Handbook DOL-224 (R-11/24): Quarterly Tax and Wage Reports (DOL-4N), domestic annual DOL-4, multiple worksite report, records
figure_or_rule_carried: DOL-4N Quarterly Tax and Wage Report due last day of month after quarter (30 Apr, 31 Jul, 31 Oct, 31 Jan); employers with 25+ employees must file and pay electronically; channels: Employer Portal direct entry (<=100 employees), Internet Wage File Upload CSV/Excel (100-15,000), SFTP (>15,000 and payroll service providers); paper DOL-4N allowed below 25 employees. Wages reported in the quarter actually paid. Domestic-only employers: annual DOL-4 by 31 January with quarterly wages (34-8-150). Multiple Worksite Report quarterly (statistical supplement). Corrections on DOL-3C. Records (34-8-121): full name and full SSN, hire/rehire dates, separation date and reason, quarterly wages incl. cash value of other remuneration and tips; retain >= 7 years. Rate notices DOL-626 posted to Employer Portal by 31 December (no longer mailed).

instrument_name: GDOL Employer Handbook DOL-224 (R-11/24): UI coverage, wages defined, non-covered employment, rate computation
figure_or_rule_carried: Liability: private employer with 1+ worker in 20 weeks or 1,500 payroll in a quarter; agricultural 10+ workers in 20 weeks or 20,000 cash in a quarter; domestic 1,000 cash in a quarter; 501(c)(3) 4+ workers in 20 weeks; government reports quarterly (mostly reimbursing). Corporate officers are employees. Wages include bonuses, board and lodging (minimum value by GDOL rule), vacation pay, tips (to FUTA extent), employee 401(k) deferrals; not wages: employer 401(k), Section 125 premiums (employer and employee), WC payments, accounted business expenses. Non-covered: sole proprietor's parent/spouse/children under 21, elected officials, casual labor < 50, student nurses, newspaper carriers < 18, commission-only insurance and real-estate agents, students in work-study programs, church/religious-order employees, inmates, certain direct sellers. New employer 2.7% until 36 months chargeable; experienced rate from reserve ratio (taxes - charges)/3-yr average payroll at 30 June computation date, statutory tables; voluntary contributions within 30 days of notice. Common paymaster allowed. SUTA dumping penalty: highest rate + >= 2 points, 4 years.

instrument_name: GDOL Employer Handbook DOL-224 (R-11/24): Separation Notice DOL-800 (O.C.G.A. 34-8-190(c), GDOL Rule 300-2-7-.06) and Mass Separation Notice DOL-402
figure_or_rule_carried: DOL-800 Separation Notice (form R-02-24) required for every separated worker regardless of reason, stating the reason; delivered on the last day of work, or mailed to the last known address within 3 days of the separation occurring or becoming known. Mass Separation Notice DOL-402 + DOL-402A to GDOL within 48 hours when 25+ workers separated same day for the same reason (lack of work) for 7+ days, or in a labor dispute. Vacation pay: no state law, matter of agreement (FLSA silent). Sales representative commissions paid within 30 days after termination of the representation agreement (non-waivable).

instrument_name: GDOL Employer Handbook DOL-224 (R-11/24): Wage and hour requirements (minimum wage, overtime, frequency, methods, deductions, garnishment, new hire, child labor)
figure_or_rule_carried: Most employers follow federal minimum wage 7.25/h; Georgia minimum wage 5.15/h applies only in rare cases not covered by FLSA. Overtime: FLSA rules (over 40/workweek at 1.5x); no state daily overtime. Frequency: semi-monthly or more frequent, except officers/superintendents/heads paid monthly. Methods: money, check, or credit transfer (direct deposit) with consent; payroll cards; full net amount; at least one free access. Deductions: no Georgia law listing permitted voluntary deductions or requiring written consent (written authorization recommended); no law against requiring purchase of uniforms/tools (FLSA floor applies). Garnishment: generally one attachment at a time, but child support order and tax levy may run simultaneously. New hire: O.C.G.A. 19-11-9.2 and 42 USC 653a, report new hires and rehires within 10 days of hire to the Georgia New Hire Reporting Program (ga-newhire.com), incl. one-day workers and returns after layoff/leave. Child labor: Employment Certificate DOL-4103 (work permit) kept on the work site for all workers under 18; minors in entertainment DOL-4101; under-16 barred from mills, factories, laundries etc.; most-protective of state/federal applies.

instrument_name: Georgia HB 463 (2026), 'Georgia Economic Growth and Tax Relief Act of 2026', as passed House and Senate (HB 463/AP)
figure_or_rule_carried: Rate 4.99% for taxable years beginning on/after 2026-01-01 (was 5.19%); reduced by 0.125 point annually from 2027-01-01 until 3.99%, each step delayed one year if any OPB trigger (revenue estimate < +3%, net revenue not above each of prior 3 years, Revenue Shortfall Reserve insufficient) holds at 1 December; OPB reports by 1 December. Standard deduction 30,000 MFJ / 15,000 single-HoH-MFS, +750 / +375 annually from 2027 to 36,000 / 18,000 (same delay triggers). Dependent exemption 5,000, +125 annually from 2027 to 6,000. Qualified overtime (IRC s.225) up to 1,750 for full-time hourly employees 2026-2028 (repealed 2028-12-31); cash tips up to 1,750 from 2026; employers report totals and employee counts monthly/quarterly with withholding returns (2026 may be annual). Act effective on Governor's approval, applicable to taxable years beginning on/after 2026-01-01. ENACTMENT: in force - signed by the Governor 2026-05-11 (GA DOR guide 2026, US-GA-001/US-GAS5-004) and the identical file (md5 match) is published by the Office of the Governor under '2026 signed legislation' (https://gov.georgia.gov/document/2026-signed-legislation/hb-463/download, read 2026-11-02); Act number not read. instrument_name: Georgia Form G-4 Employee's Withholding Allowance Certificate (Rev. 06/03/26)

instrument_name: Georgia SB 160 (2023), Act 86, as passed: O.C.G.A. 34-8-151 new-employer contribution rate schedule and 34-8-155 sunset dates

instrument_name: Iowa Code 2026 sec. 91D.1 Minimum wage requirements
figure_or_rule_carried: State hourly wage 7.25 from 2008-01-01, or the federal minimum if greater; first 90 calendar days of employment: at least 6.35/h; tip credit (restaurant, hotel, motel, inn, cabin; more than 30/month in tips) up to 40% of the applicable minimum wage, employee may appeal to DIAL; FLSA 29 USC 213 exemptions apply; enterprises under 300,000 annual gross volume exempt except laundering, construction, hospitals/care/schools and public agencies. No scheduled increase in the Iowa Code 2026 text.

instrument_name: Iowa Code 2026 sec. 91A.3 Mode of payment
figure_or_rule_carried: Pay at least monthly, semimonthly or biweekly on regular paydays designated in advance; payday not more than 12 days (excluding Sundays and legal holidays) after the end of the period; written agreement may vary; commissions may be paid as a credit with true-up at intervals of at most 12 months. Payment in US currency or negotiable instrument unless written consent to pay in kind. Direct deposit by employee election; employees hired on/after 2005-07-01 may be required to use direct deposit unless account costs push wages below minimum wage, account fees result, or a CBA prohibits it. Mail on written request (keep the request 2 years after). Overdraft charges from late pay recoverable. Expenses reimbursed in advance or within 30 days of the claim.

instrument_name: Iowa Code 2026 sec. 91A.4 Employment suspension or termination - how wages are paid
figure_or_rule_carried: On suspension or termination (no discharge/resignation distinction) all wages earned are due not later than the next regular payday for the period in which earned; commission true-up within 30 days; vacation payable only if due under an agreement or employer policy establishing pro rata accrual, prorated to the fraction of the year worked.

instrument_name: Iowa Code 2026 sec. 91A.5 Deductions from wages
figure_or_rule_carried: Deduction only if required/permitted by state or federal law or court order, or with written employee authorization for a lawful purpose benefiting the employee. Prohibited: shared till shortages (except one written manager agreement per establishment, 45 days), dishonoured checks within discretion, breakage/damage/customer default unless willful, lost/stolen property unless assigned equipment acknowledged in writing, gratuities, PPE (other than off-duty clothing/footwear) unless CBA, relocation costs over 20 for 91E.1 employers.

P: daily 260, weekly 52, biweekly 26, semimonthly 24, monthly 12, annual 1; other frequencies annualise. Pre-tax retirement and health contributions excluded from taxable wages. instrument_name: Iowa Code 2026 sec. 422.5 Tax imposed (individual income tax rate)

instrument_name: Iowa Code 2026 sec. 422.16 Withholding of income tax at source (deposit, return and W-2 provisions)
figure_or_rule_carried: Withhold from Iowa residents and nonresidents working in Iowa. Quarterly return due the last day of the month after the quarter. Deposits: quarterly if under 6,000/yr and at most 500/month; monthly if over 500 in any month and at most 5,000 per semimonthly period, due the 15th of the following month (3rd month with the quarterly return); semimonthly if over 5,000 per semimonthly period, 1st-15th due the 25th, 16th-end due the 10th of the next month; annual election for at most 2 employees with written consent, paid with the Q1 return. Income statement (W-2) to the employee by January 31 (terminated employee on request within 30 days of last payment).

Filing frequencies: quarterly < 6,000/yr (< 500/month); monthly 6,000-120,000/yr; semimonthly > 120,000/yr (> 5,000 per semimonthly period); every period filed even if zero; monthly = 2 payments + quarterly return; semimonthly = 6 payments + quarterly return; returns electronic via GovConnectIowa. Withholding credits (260E NJC 1.5%/3%, SJC 1.5%, 260G ACE up to 10%, TJC 3%) on a credit schedule of the quarterly return. W-2 to employees by end of January; e-file W-2/1099 with Iowa withholding by February 15. NRA additional withholding guidance: 15,000 (or 29,200) / pay periods x 3.8%. Exemption thresholds for the IA W-4: 13,500 MFJ/HoH, 9,000 single (under 65); 32,000/24,000 at 65+.

instrument_name: Idaho State Tax Commission - Withholding Filing (Form 910 cycles) and Due Dates
authority: Idaho State Tax Commission (Wayback id_ 20260618173701 and 20260412130751)
article_or_section: Form 910 filing cycles; due dates chart (https://tax.idaho.gov/taxes/income-tax/withholding/withholding-due-dates/)
figure_or_rule_carried: Form 910 filed online in TAP. Semimonthly: withhold >= 25,000/month or >= 300,000 in 12 months; due 20th (for 1st-15th) and 5th of next month (16th-end). Monthly: < 25,000/month and > 750/quarter, or one monthly pay period; due 20th of following month. Quarterly: <= 750/quarter, or farmer filing with IDOL; due last day of month after quarter. Annual: < 750/year, or farmer not filing with IDOL; due last day of January. Zero return required. Report by date wages paid. Cycle set for full calendar year; change request by Nov 15. PEOs may file under PEO EIN. Form ID-POA needed for preparers. Weekend/holiday -> next business day.

instrument_name: Idaho Code 32-1210 Employer's duties and responsibilities - Fee for employer (child support income withholding)
figure_or_rule_carried: Court IWO: answer within 10 days of service. Withhold immediately on receipt; remit to the Department of Health and Welfare within 7 business days after the pay date. Multiple orders: send all to the Department; current support first, pro rata among obligees, excess pro rata to arrears. Notify termination with last address and new employer. Employer fee up to USD 5 per withholding, inside the 50% cap. Snapshot dated 2025-02-06 (no later capture checked).

instrument_name: Idaho State Tax Commission - Withholding: Types of Employees
authority: Idaho State Tax Commission (Wayback id_ 20260514201525; page last updated 2022-08-30)
article_or_section: Corporate officers; statutory employees; family; domestic; farm; out-of-state
figure_or_rule_carried: Corporate officers are employees. Federal statutory employees: no Idaho withholding required. Family members: withhold as others. Domestic employees: wages taxable, employer must hold a withholding account, report wages, issue W-2 and file 967, but withholding not required. Farm help: withhold if federal withholding required and employee earns >= 1,000 in the year; Form 910 quarterly if filing IDOL reports, else annually. Nonresidents physically working in Idaho: withhold if they earn > 1,000 in Idaho in the year; report all Idaho wages on W-2. Out-of-state employer with an employee physically in Idaho must withhold; no Idaho withholding for work not physically in Idaho (voluntary for Idaho residents). Idaho residents working elsewhere: all income taxable in Idaho, withholding optional. Employee/contractor test follows federal.

instrument_name: Idaho Department of Labor - Unemployment Insurance Tax Information Handbook for Businesses (rev. 2025-11-05)
article_or_section: Who must pay; quarterly reports TX20/TX26/TX20C; standard rate; taxable wage base; corporate officers; claiming wages in another state; exempt services
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly UI report and payment due last day of month after quarter end (72-1311), no grace period, weekend/holiday -> next workday; online filing mandatory via Employer Portal (paper TX20/TX26 only on approved written request); zero reports required; amendments on TX20C in the quarter of error. Idaho Business Registration within 6 months of becoming covered (penalty up to 500). New employers: standard rate at least 6 quarters. Wage base: notice each year, set from average annual wage; wages paid to the same worker in another state count toward the Idaho base only if tax was paid to that state (72-1349(1)). Corporate officers reportable; may opt out by form before March 31. Domestic: coverage on cash wages, tax on cash and noncash; agricultural: cash and cash-equivalent only; H-2A wages count for coverage but are not taxed. 28 pages; the coverage chart on p.3 is an image (not extracted).

instrument_name: Idaho Code 72-1315 Covered employer

Domestic service in private home/college club/fraternity: cash wages >= 1,000 in a quarter. Governmental entities and nonprofits covered. LLC follows federal classification; LLC taxed as corporation -> members are corporate officers. Last am. 2025 ch. 29.

article_or_section: When is my Form IL-941 due; payment frequency; electronic requirements; corrections

W-2/W-2c/W-2G must be submitted electronically. Over-withholding corrected in a later quarter of the same year; after W-2 issued do not refund or amend withholding.

article_or_section: When is compensation paid in Illinois; Limited exceptions; When am I not required to withhold; Form IL-W-6
figure_or_rule_carried: Compensation paid in Illinois = service localized in IL (all in IL, or out-of-state service incidental). No IL withholding (absent voluntary agreement) on: residents of IA, KY, MI, WI (reciprocity); qualifying military spouses (VBTA 2018); nonresident with fewer than 31 days of service in IL whose compensation is not localized in IL (IL-W-6 certificate of days worked kept on file for nonresidents expected to work >30 days without time-and-attendance system); nonresident working entirely in another state; IL resident working entirely in another state where compensation is subject to that state's withholding; payments under IRC 3405/3406; STB rail/motor carrier nonresidents in more than one state; air carrier nonresidents with <=50% of compensation (flight miles) in IL; vessel crew; compensation exempt from federal withholding (e.g. certain ministers); household employees (unless federal voluntary withholding agreement exists - then IL withholding required; report on IL-1040 Line 20 or IL-941; Pub. 121). instrument_name: IDOL Paid Leave for All Workers Act FAQ (820 ILCS 192; 56 Ill. Adm. Code 200)
figure_or_rule_carried: PLAWA (eff. 2024-01-01): 1 hour paid leave per 40 hours worked, up to 40 hours per 12-month period (or frontload; part-time pro rata frontload); usable after 90 days of employment, for any reason; only hours actually worked count; FLSA-exempt employees deemed to work 40 hours/week (or regular shorter week); carryover of unused accrued leave allowed (not for frontloaded leave); no payout at year-end unless mutually agreed in writing annually (200.320(d)); no payout at separation UNLESS the leave is part of a vacation or general PTO bank (then IWPCA payout applies); frontloaded leave cannot be recouped on early separation; paid at regular rate, tipped and commissioned employees at least the full local minimum wage ($15 state) or base rate if higher. Does not apply in Chicago or Cook County, which had paid leave ordinances before 2024-01-01; later local ordinances must comply with PLAWA. Exemptions include part-time college/university students employed by their school and some short-term higher-education temporaries; staffing agencies covered.

Annual caps, carryover and separation payout rules for paid leave by employer size are in the BACP FAQ PDF, which returned 403 (ACCESS gap).

instrument_name: Illinois HFS Child Support Services: Income Withholding for Support employer guidance (305 ILCS 5/10-16.2; 750 ILCS 28)
authority: Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
article_or_section: Employer Compliance; Withholding Calculations; Multiple Orders
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers honour federal-standard Order/Notice - Income Withholding for Support from any state (Illinois form HFS 3683, cover letter HFS 3598, National Medical Support Notice HFS 3554); served by first-class/certified mail, fax/electronic, personal delivery. Employer may deduct and retain up to $5 per month fee from the employee's remaining income. Remit 1 to 7 business days after payday as instructed. Withhold up to 50% of disposable income (gross minus mandatory deductions) when the full ordered amount cannot be withheld (HFS 3683 instruction; within CCPA limits). Multiple orders, different children: allocate per Illinois law, not first-come first-served (HFS allocation calculator); same child: honour only the first order. Report termination on the 'Notification of Employment Termination or Income Status' section.

instrument_name: 735 ILCS 5/12-803 Wages subject to collection (wage deduction orders), ILGA public file repository
figure_or_rule_carried: Non-support creditor wage deduction order: amount subject to collection per work week = lesser of (1) 15% of GROSS wages, salary, commissions and bonuses for the week, or (2) disposable earnings for the week minus 45 x the greater of the federal minimum hourly wage or the Illinois minimum wage (820 ILCS 105/4) in effect when payable. Derivation 2026: 45 x $15.00 = $675.00 protected weekly floor (federal floor 45 x 7.25 = 326.25 is lower). Applies irrespective of where earned or where the employee resides. Disposable earnings = earnings after amounts required by law to be withheld. Source P.A. 94-306 eff. 2006-01-01; 95-661 eff. 2008-01-01.

instrument_name: Indiana Minimum Wage Law of 1965, IC 22-2-2-3 and 22-2-2-4 (IC 2026, Title 22 Art. 2)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer = 2+ employees in a workweek and NOT subject to FLSA minimum wage. 22-2-2-4(c): minimum wage = the FLSA minimum wage (no own figure; 7.25 USD/h federal). (d) tip credit: cash wage not less than 2.13 USD/h, employer supports tip credit by reported tips. (f) overtime 1.5x regular rate over 40 h/workweek; no daily overtime; (n) domestic service also 40 h rule. Exempt from the state law: persons under 16; agricultural labour; student nurses/students working for own school; religious-order members and ministers; commission-only employees; executives earning 150+/week; persons employed no more than 4 weeks in any 4 consecutive 3-month periods; motor carrier; direct sellers; minor-league baseball (22-2-2-3(a)-(r)).

instrument_name: IC 22-2-2-10.5 Prohibition against unit establishing a higher minimum wage; IC 22-2-16-3 prohibition on local benefit/leave mandates

A unit may not mandate any benefit, term of employment, working condition or attendance/scheduling/leave policy exceeding federal/state law (IC 22-2-16-3, P.L.88-2013, amended P.L.120-2016): no local paid sick leave ordinances; does not apply to a unit's own employees or to unit contracts/incentive terms (22-2-16-1).

Voluntary leaver: paid at the next usual and regular payday; if whereabouts unknown, penalty not triggered until 10 business days after demand or address furnished. FLSA-overtime-eligible salaried employees exempt from s.1 (1.1). Failure: unpaid wages + attorney fee; if not in good faith, liquidated damages 2x the wages due (22-2-5-2, P.L.193-2015). Farmers/agriculture exempt from the chapter (22-2-5-3).

instrument_name: IC 22-2-6 Wage deductions (wage assignments, overpayment recovery), two 2026 versions (P.L.104-2026 s.22 and P.L.115-2026 s.14)
figure_or_rule_carried: Any employee-directed deduction = wage assignment, valid only if written, signed by employee, revocable on written notice, agreed in writing by employer, copy delivered to employer within 10 days, and for a listed purpose (insurance, charity, US bonds, employer stock, union dues, employer merchandise, employer loan, health/pension plans, credit union, uniforms/tools at direct cost, training reimbursement, payroll/vacation advance, etc.). Interest on employer loans/advances <= Fed prime + 4%. Uniform/tool assignments capped at lesser of 2,500 USD/year or 5% of weekly disposable earnings; no charge for OSHA PPE. Overpayment recovery: 2 weeks notice; cap lesser of 25% of weekly disposable earnings or excess over 30x federal minimum hourly wage; decimal-point error of 10x gross may be recovered at once (22-2-6-4). Two versions in IC 2026: P.L.104-2026 adds (b)(19) political-subdivision deferred retirement (opt-out, no (a) formalities); P.L.115-2026 re-points UCCC refs IC 24-4.5 -> IC 37-2/37-3 (consumer-credit recodification). instrument_name: Indiana DOR Departmental Notice #1, Effective Oct. 1, 2026 (R47 / 10-26): How to Compute Withholding for State and County Income Tax
article_or_section: pp.1-5 (deduction constant Tables A/B/C, example, nonresident 30-day rule, county rate chart)
figure_or_rule_carried: State AGI rate 2026 2.95%. Method: taxable = gross per period - deduction constants (WH-4 line 5 personal exemptions 1,000/yr each incl. 65+/blind; lines 6 and 7 dependent and first-time dependent 1,500/yr each; line 8 adopted child 3,000/yr; constants = annual amount / pay periods: weekly 52, biweekly 26, semimonthly 24, monthly 12, daily 365) x 2.95% state, x county rate county tax. County of residence on Jan 1, or if out-of-state resident on Jan 1, county of principal work on Jan 1. Nonresident 30-day rule (from 2024-01-01): no state/county withholding if employee expected to work in Indiana 30 days or less (time-and-attendance system or Form WH-4AFF), catch-up if exceeded; not for athletes/entertainers/public figures or part-year residents. instrument_name: Indiana DOR Income Tax Information Bulletin #32, General Information on Local Income Taxes (Dec 2024)
figure_or_rule_carried: Local Income Tax (LIT) replaced CAGIT/COIT/CEDIT from tax year 2017; all 92 counties have a LIT. County of residence and county of principal business/employment fixed as of Jan 1 for the whole year; a mid-year move requires a new WH-4 but only sets the county for the next year. Residents: county rate on whole Indiana AGI; nonresidents with principal work in an Indiana county: same rate on income derived from that county; reciprocity does not apply to county tax; no separate nonresident LIT rate. Rate caps: expenditure rate up to 2.5% (2.75% Marion), +1.25% property tax relief, special purpose rates (IC 6-3.6-5/-6/-7). Rate-change timing: ordinance Jan 1-Aug 31 -> effective Oct 1 same year; Sep 1-Oct 31 -> Jan 1 next year; Nov 1-Dec 31 -> Oct 1 next year. 30-day nonresident safe harbor IC 6-3-2-27.5 from 2024 (employees only; not team members, entertainers, contractors). Credit against county tax for out-of-state local tax (residents only).

instrument_name: Indiana DCS Child Support Bureau: Indiana's Income Withholding Law, employer FAQ
authority: Indiana Department of Child Services, Child Support Bureau
figure_or_rule_carried: Applies to all employers regardless of size; IWO for child support only. Withholding begins no later than the first pay period occurring within 14 days after the IWO was mailed/faxed/served; remit to INSCCU each time the employee is paid. Employer with 50+ employees and more than one employee with an order must remit electronically. CCPA limits 50% / 55% (other dependents, under/over 12 weeks arrears) and 60% / 65% (no other dependents). Disposable earnings = after legally required deductions (taxes, social security); voluntary deductions and union dues stay in. Priority: child support over any other claim except current federal, state and local taxes; business garnishments limited to the remaining room under the 25% Indiana/CCPA limit. Lump sums (severance, accumulated sick/vacation pay, commissions, bonus) subject to arrears withholding up to the CCPA limit (contact EMU). Multiple IWOs prorated (DCS Prorate Calculator). Employer fee: optional 2.00 USD per withholding forwarded to INSCCU (inside the CCPA limit: if limit reached, remit limit minus 2.00). Annual Support Fee (ASFE) IWO counts within CCPA limit. Employer liable for amounts not withheld; up to 5,000 USD civil recovery for retaliation. NMSN for health coverage. Independent-contractor payments also subject to IWO.

instrument_name: KRS 337.020 Time of payment of wages

instrument_name: KRS 337.055 Final pay on dismissal or voluntary leaving

instrument_name: KRS 337.010 Definitions (wages incl. vested vacation pay; payment methods; minimum-wage exclusions)
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages include vested vacation pay, overtime, severance, earned bonuses; payable in legal tender, checks, direct deposits or payroll card accounts (no activation fee; at least 1 free withdrawal per pay period up to full balance). Min-wage/overtime (KRS 337.275-.325) exclude: agriculture; exec/admin/professional/outside sales; federal employees; domestic service in a private home (unless more than one domestic regularly employed); certificated learners/apprentices/students/disabled workers; retail/service/hotel/restaurant under 95,000 USD gross for 5 years or family members; babysitters/companions; newspaper delivery; state employees under KRS 7,16,27A,30A,18A; seasonal camps; residential carers; direct sellers (IRC 3508(b)(2)); contracted baseball players. instrument_name: KRS 337.060 Withholding of wages and prohibited deductions
figure_or_rule_carried: No deduction from agreed wage unless authorised by local/state/federal law or expressly authorised in writing by the employee (insurance, medical dues, etc.); union dues only with written consent for CBAs from 2017-01-09; never deduct fines, common-till cash shortages, breakage, dishonoured checks (where employee has discretion), or losses from faulty work/theft/damage/customer default unless wilful.

instrument_name: KRS 337.065 Gratuities and tip pooling

instrument_name: KRS 341.030 Wages defined; taxable wage base and trust-fund trigger
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base 8,000 then 9,000 from 2012-01-01, +300 each January 1 up to a cap of 12,000; increase suspended/limited when the trust fund balance on Sept 30 is below/near 200,000,000 (7)(b)-(f); 2021-2022 increase suspended. instrument_name: DOR Withholding Tax Guide (posted August 2026)
figure_or_rule_carried: Withhold from residents (services in or outside MA) and nonresidents (services in MA); non-MA employer with MA office: MA amount minus own-state amount; no federal withholding required -> no MA withholding (household employers generally not required, optional). Percentage method: wages minus FICA/Medicare/MA-US-RR retirement contributions (annual max 2,000) minus exemption amount (daily 3n+9; weekly 19n+66; biweekly 38n+131; semimonthly 42n+141; monthly 83n+284; annual 1,000n+3,400) x withholding rate; HoH/blind reductions weekly 2.31/2.12, biweekly 4.62/4.23, semimonthly 5.00/4.58, monthly 10.00/9.17, daily 0.33/0.30. Return/payment: <=100 annual (Jan 31); 101-1,200 quarterly; 1,201-25,000 monthly by 15th (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec due last day of next month); >25,000 quarterly return + payment within 3 business days when >=500 accumulated by 7th/15th/22nd/last day. E-file mandatory: new registrations, payroll service providers, combined liability >=5,000. Records 3 years. New hires within 2 weeks; contractors >=600. W-2 to employees by Jan 31. Page also states 50+ employees file W-2 machine-readable by last day of March and paper W-2 + M-3/M-3M by Feb 28 (CONFLICTS with US-MAS5-015). Annual exemption 3,200 (weekly 61.54, biweekly 123.08, semimonthly 133.33, monthly 266.67, quarterly 800, daily 8.77); standard deduction 3,400 flat (weekly 65.38, biweekly 130.76, semimonthly 141.66, monthly 283.33, quarterly 850, daily 9.31: guide truncates, not rounds). Tables ignore the 2/3/4% bands (start at 4.75%). Ten local tables (2.25, 2.40, 2.65, 2.75, 2.85, 3.00, 3.05, 3.10, 3.20, 3.30): use the table that equals or slightly exceeds the county rate. Combined rate = state band + local; e.g. 3.30 table single annual 8.05% to 100,000, then 8.30/8.55/8.80/9.05/9.55/9.80%; lump-sum annual bonus at 6.50% + county top local rate (9.80% at 3.30). Nonresident (nonreciprocal state): state + special 2.25%, no local; MD residents working in DE/nonreciprocal states: Delaware table (3.30% flat in the extract). No withholding below per-period floors (weekly 96, biweekly 192, semimonthly 208, monthly 417, daily 13.70, annual 5,000). Single/student low-income exemption thresholds (annual 15,750 under 65 / 17,750 65+). Not withheld: domestic service in a private home, ministers/religious orders, nonresident seamen, employees paid <5,000/yr. No certificate: withhold as one exemption. Filing categories: accelerated (>=15,000 prior year and >=700 accumulated: within 3 business days of pay date), monthly (>700 in a quarter: 15th of following month), quarterly (<700/quarter), seasonal, annual (<250/yr, by 31 January). MW506 via Maryland Tax Connect; MW508 + W-2 by 31 January; records 3 years; penalty up to 25%. Gambling >5,000: 9.50% resident / 8.75% nonresident; rollover distributions 7.75%.

instrument_name: Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act, 2018 PA 337 as amended by 2025 PA 1 (MCL 408.931-408.945), compiled through PA 114 of 2026
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum hourly wage 12.48 from 2025-02-21; 13.73 from 2026-01-01; 15.00 from 2027-01-01 (enacted). From October 2027 the State Treasurer indexes by 12-month Midwest CPI-U, published by 1 November, effective 1 January following; no increase if MI unemployment >= 8.5% the preceding year. Employer = 2+ employees; employee = 16 years or older. Act does not apply to FLSA-covered employers unless the federal minimum is lower (408.940(1)); companionship and non-live-in childcare workers covered (408.940(2)).

instrument_name: Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act sec. 4a overtime and compensatory time (MCL 408.934a)
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime 1.5x regular rate over 40 hours in a workweek; public hospital 8/80 option by written agreement; exemptions: bona fide executive/administrative/professional, seasonal amusement (<=7 months), agriculture, employees not subject to the minimum wage. Compensatory time in lieu of overtime at 1.5 hours per hour, cap 240 hours, cash out within 30 days of request, unused comp time paid at termination; comp time earned/paid must appear on the statement of earnings (408.934a(8)(d)(ii)). Civil fine up to 1,000.

instrument_name: Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act secs. 4b and 4d: training, minor and tipped minimum wages (MCL 408.934b, 408.934d)
figure_or_rule_carried: Training wage 4.25/hour for first 90 days, new employee under 20; under-18 minimum = 85% of general minimum (2026: 13.73 x 0.85 = 11.6705, derived). Tipped minimum = % of general minimum: 38% from 2025-02-21, 40% from 2026-01-01 (13.73 x 0.40 = 5.492, derived), 42% 2027, 44% 2028, 46% 2029, 48% 2030, 50% 2031; conditions: tips cover the gap, FICA-declared, retained by employee (pooling only in chain of service), written notice and written consent at hire; service-charge distribution notice; records 3 years after last pay period; civil fine up to 2,500.

instrument_name: Earned Sick Time Act, 2018 PA 338 as amended by 2025 PA 2 (MCL 408.961-408.974), compiled through PA 114 of 2026
figure_or_rule_carried: Every employer (1+ employees). Accrual 1 hour per 30 hours worked (PTO hours excluded). Small business (10 or fewer working in a week; not small if >10 on payroll in 20+ workweeks of current/prior year): usage cap 40 hours/year, carry-over cap 40, or frontload 40; small-business obligations start 2025-10-01. Others: usage cap 72 hours/year, carry-over cap 72, or frontload 72; part-time proportional frontload with written notice of expected hours. Exempt (FLSA 13(a)(1)) employees assumed 40 h/week. Pay at greater of normal hourly/base wage or state minimum (overtime, holiday pay, bonuses, commissions, piece rate, tips excluded). Use in 1-hour or smallest increment; new hires may be made to wait 120 calendar days. Frontloading employers need not carry over, track or pay out. Not paid out at separation (408.965(3)); rehire within 2 months reinstates unused balance unless paid out. PTO policy of equal amount complies. Excluded: federal employees, self-scheduling workers, unpaid interns, youth-employment-standards minors. Records of hours worked and sick time 3 years (408.970). Civil fine up to 8x normal hourly wage; posting violation up to 100.

instrument_name: Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act, 1978 PA 390, sec. 2 (MCL 408.472) pay frequency and timing
figure_or_rule_carried: Default semi-monthly: wages for days 1-15 paid by the 1st of the next month; days 16-end paid by the 15th of the next month. Weekly or biweekly regular payday complies if payday is on or before the 14th day after the end of the work period. Monthly pay period complies if paid within 15 days after period end. December overtime may be paid on the next regular payday. Hand harvesters: by the 2nd day after the work week. Employer = 1+ employees.

instrument_name: Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act sec. 6 (MCL 408.476) method of payment: direct deposit and payroll debit card
figure_or_rule_carried: Methods: cash; negotiable check payable without discount; direct deposit/electronic transfer; payroll debit card meeting (6). Direct deposit and paycard need full, free, written consent, EXCEPT employer may mandate direct deposit or paycard if it gives a written election form (DD or paycard), a statement that failure to return the form within 30 days = consent to paycard (not for those already on DD), and paycard disclosures (fees, free access, ATM charges, free balance, right to change, no bank account). Employee may change method at any time, implemented within 1 pay period. Paycard: 1 free withdrawal per pay period, 21 days notice of fee changes, unlimited free balance inquiries, no credit link. Employer may not pass payment-method costs to the employee.

instrument_name: Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act secs. 3-5 and 10 (MCL 408.473-408.475, 408.480) final pay, fringe benefits (vacation), deceased employee
figure_or_rule_carried: Final pay: voluntary quit - all wages earned and due as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined (hand harvesters: within 3 days); discharge - immediately, as soon as the amount can with due diligence be determined; contract workers - estimated wages per sec. 2, final payment at contract end. Fringe benefits (holiday, sick, personal, vacation, bonuses, expenses, contributions) are paid per the written contract or written policy (408.471(e), 408.473): accrued-vacation payout at termination follows the written policy, no statutory payout. Fringe benefit due at termination may be withheld only by written contract or signed free consent (408.474). Deceased employee: wages/fringe to written designee if no letters of administration, else spouse, children, parents, siblings in that order; payment discharges the employer.

instrument_name: Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act sec. 7 (MCL 408.477) wage deductions
figure_or_rule_carried: No deduction without full, free, written consent except those required/expressly permitted by law or CBA. Deduction for the employer benefit: written consent for EACH wage payment and may not take gross below the state minimum wage (charitable deductions to a 501(c)(3) employer: one consent). Each deduction substantiated per employee; no prorating. Overpayment recovery without consent within 6 months if clerical/math error, written explanation 1 pay period before, max 15% of gross for the period, taken after all other deductions, not below the greater of state/FLSA minimum. Same 15% rule for an employer-paid default judgment under MCL 600.4012(9)/(10). Complaint within 12 months.

instrument_name: Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act sec. 9 (MCL 408.479) records and wage statement; IWOWA sec. 7 (MCL 408.937)
figure_or_rule_carried: Record per employee: name, address, birth date, occupation/classification, total basic rate of pay, total hours each pay period, total wages each pay period, separate itemization of deductions, listing of fringe benefits; kept 3 years. Statement at time of payment: hours worked, gross wages paid, pay period identification, separate itemization of deductions (piece-rate hand harvesters: units). Hours need not be recorded/stated for bona fide executive, administrative, professional employees, elected officials, political appointees. Statute is silent on electronic delivery (no consent rule located). IWOWA 408.937 repeats: statement of hours, wages and deductions each pay period. Re-read of the act text; complements US-MIP51-005 / US-MIL-002.

instrument_name: Michigan Employment Security Act sec. 44 (MCL 421.44) remuneration, wages and taxable wage limit
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage limit 9,500 per employee per calendar year; reduced to 9,000 for the whole year for non-delinquent employers when the fund balance on 30 June of the prior year is >= 2.5 billion and projected to stay there (statutory mechanism behind the 2026 9,000 base in US-MIP51-004; delinquent = quarterly unpaid balance >= 25, cured if paid within 45 days of the first quarter). Not indexed (fixed amounts). Wages include FICA-reported tips; wages paid by the same employer in other states count toward the limit; successor counts predecessor wages. Excluded from wages: retirement/sickness/medical plan payments, 401(a)/403(a) trust payments, employer-paid employee FICA, non-cash pay outside the trade or business, deductible moving expenses, SUB plan payments, National Guard pay. Remuneration not received within 21 days after period end deemed paid on day 21.

instrument_name: Michigan Employment Security Act sec. 43 (MCL 421.43) services excluded from employment (UI coverage of special populations)
figure_or_rule_carried: Excluded from UI employment: H-2A agricultural aliens; agricultural labor unless the employer meets sec. 41(5); domestic service in a private home unless employer meets sec. 41(6); service for son, daughter or spouse and child under 18 for a parent; commission-only real estate, investment and insurance agents; 501(c)(3)-type exempt orgs if under 50 in the quarter; students employed by their school (normally <=30 h/week) and spouses with notice; under-22 co-op students in a certified program; newspaper delivery under 18; for-profit employers: minor students below college level working less than scheduled hours / in school vacations / in accredited curriculum, college students in accredited curriculum; direct sellers; product demonstrators meeting the test; AmeriCorps; landmen. Church employment excluded for sec. 42(8)-(10) purposes.

instrument_name: Michigan Employment Security Act sec. 19 (MCL 421.19) contribution rates: new and construction employers
figure_or_rule_carried: New employer rate 2.7% in years 1 and 2 of liability (then phased in with the chargeable benefits component in years 3-4/5); construction employers pay the average construction contractor rate determined by the agency in years 1-2, then phased. Rate components (CBC, ABC, NBC) as in US-MIP9W-002. Statutory basis for the 2.7% in US-MIP51-003; employer-only contributions (no employee UI contribution in MI: US-FEDP52-006 lists AK, NJ, PA only).

instrument_name: Social Security Number Privacy Act, 2004 PA 454 (MCL 445.81-445.87)
figure_or_rule_carried: A person may not intentionally publicly display, print on badges/cards, use as primary account number, transmit over an unsecured connection, or include visibly through an envelope, all or more than 4 sequential digits of an SSN; mailing a document with more than 4 digits is allowed where law authorises it or to service an employee benefit. Uses authorised or required by federal/state law (e.g. W-2) are exempt. Anyone obtaining SSNs in the ordinary course of business must adopt and publish (handbook/manual, may be electronic) a privacy policy: confidentiality, no unlawful disclosure, access limits, disposal, penalties. Payroll effect: pay statement shows at most the last 4 digits.

instrument_name: Local Government Labor Regulatory Limitation Act, 2015 PA 105 (MCL 123.1381-123.1396)
figure_or_rule_carried: Local governments may not require a minimum wage above the state minimum, local prevailing wage/fringe rates (except state projects), paid or unpaid leave, or hours/scheduling rules (ordinances adopted after 2014-12-31). Payroll effect: no local minimum wage or local paid-leave layer in Michigan; the state minimum (US-MIS5-001) and ESTA (US-MIS5-004) are the only rates.

instrument_name: Income Tax Act of 1967 sec. 30 (MCL 206.30) taxable income, personal exemption indexation, tips and overtime deduction (subdiv. (ee) added by 2025 PA 24; compiled through 2026 PA 39)
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable income starts from federal AGI (rolling IRC conformity, so federal exclusions such as 401(k) deferrals, sec. 125, HSA, transit and group-term life flow through), with listed adjustments. Personal exemption base 3,700 indexed annually by US CPI for the state fiscal year ending in the prior tax year over FY2010-11, plus 600 from 2022, rounded to the nearest 100 (2026 value 5,900 per Guide 446). NEW: subdiv. (ee), enacted by 2025 PA 24 (signed 2025-10-07, per Treasury notice US-MIS5-017): tax years 2026-2028 deduct federally allowed qualified tips (IRC 224) and qualified overtime (IRC 225), nonresidents only for MI-sourced amounts. Level = ASSESSMENT (individual return); no withholding change located in statute, Guide 446 Rev. 02-26 or the Treasury notice. Section last amended by 2026 PA 39, imd. eff. 2026-07-22 (content of that amendment not isolated). (ff): from TY2025 AGI computed decoupled from IRC 168(n)/174A.

instrument_name: Support and Parenting Time Enforcement Act, 1982 PA 295, sec. 8 (MCL 552.608) limit on support income withholding
figure_or_rule_carried: Total income withheld under all support withholding orders (current support, arrears, fees, health-care premiums) may not exceed 50% of disposable earnings as defined in 15 USC 1672 (a flat state cap, lower than the CCPA 55/60/65% tiers for some cases).

instrument_name: Michigan Treasury Taxpayer Notice: New Deductions for Qualified Overtime Compensation and Qualified Tips (2026-01-06)
authority: Michigan Department of Treasury, Bureau of Tax Policy
article_or_section: Notice, sections Background / Tax Years Impacted / Implementation
figure_or_rule_carried: 2025 PA 24, signed 2025-10-07, amended MCL 206.30 (subdiv. (ee)): deduction of federally deducted qualified tips (IRC 224) and qualified overtime (IRC 225) for tax years 2026, 2027, 2028 only (not 2025); residents deduct all, nonresidents only amounts attributable to services in Michigan. Status: ENACTED, in force. Level: ASSESSMENT (taxable income on MI-1040); the notice contains no employer withholding instruction; further guidance may be issued. A tier-B search summary claiming employers must stop MI withholding on tips is NOT supported by this notice or Guide 446 Rev. 02-26.

instrument_name: Michigan Treasury 2026 Sales, Use and Withholding Taxes Monthly/Quarterly Return (Form 5080, Rev. 12-25) and Annual Return (Form 5081, Rev. 04-25), from the 2026 Withholding Tax Forms page
figure_or_rule_carried: Withholding is reported on the combined SUW return (one frequency for all SUW tax types on the account, assigned by Treasury): Form 5080 monthly/quarterly return due the 20th of the month following the return period; Form 5081 annual return for 2026 due 2027-02-28, reconciling total W-2/1099 count (line 17), MI tax withheld per W-2/1099 (line 18) and withholding paid (line 19a); do not attach W-2s. Late penalty 5% of tax due (+interest). Filing via MTO, approved software or paper; payments by MTO, EFT credit (Form 2329) or voucher 5094. Forms page also lists MI-W4, MI W-4P, 447 (magnetic media transmittal), 151 POA, 163 discontinuance, 3281 new hire form. Filing-frequency thresholds (incl. accelerated/EFT) NOT stated on these documents.

instrument_name: Michigan Form MI-W4 Employee Withholding Exemption Certificate (Rev. 12-20) with Guide 446 (Rev. 02-26) MI-W4 rules
figure_or_rule_carried: State certificate MI-W4 required; federal W-4 cannot substitute. Line 6 number of personal and dependency exemptions (cannot exceed MI-1040 entitlement); line 7 additional amount per pay (if employer agrees); line 8a/8b exemption from withholding (no liability; nonresident military spouse; other exempt reasons); line 5 new-hire date. No certificate = withhold on zero exemptions. Invalid/altered certificate: ignore, require new one, keep prior valid one. Employer sends copies to Treasury (Tax Technical Section, PO Box 30477) when 10+ exemptions or exempt claimed, not for reciprocal-state residents. Per-period withholding = 4.25% x (wages - exemptions x 5,900 / pay periods) (Guide 446). Nonresidency: employer-designed certificate/letter (Treasury issues none).

instrument_name: Michigan UIA Employer FAQ - Quarterly Reports (MiUI)
article_or_section: FAQ: When are quarterly reports due? / How do I complete and submit
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer Quarterly Wage/Tax Report filed in MiUI (File a Report; corrections via Wage Detail Reporting > Wage Adjustments). Due 25 January, 25 April, 25 July, 25 October; if the 25th is a weekend/holiday, next business day. MiUI Release 1 (Tax) go-live 2026-02-23 per US-MIP51-004. File format/specification for bulk wage files not read (see MiUI quarterly wage report testing page, open question).

instrument_name: Michigan Treasury Withholding Tax page (Due Dates) and Accelerated EFT Filers page
figure_or_rule_carried: Treasury assigns monthly, quarterly or annual frequency each year; monthly due the 20th of the following month; quarterly due 20 April / 20 July / 20 October / 20 January; annual 28 February following year; all filers also file the annual return by 28 February. Weekend/state holiday: next business day. Accelerated EFT: withholding liability of 480,000 or more in the previous calendar year (sales/use 720,000) -> withholding remitted by EFT (credit or debit) on or before the same day as the federal deposit, regardless of amount; Treasury notifies in April, change effective July. Withholding calculator listed under Estimators and Calculators (oracle: www.michigan.gov/taxes/business-taxes/withholding/tax-calculator per Guide 446).

instrument_name: Michigan UIA MiUI Quarterly Wage Report file format reference documents (Delimited v3, EFW2 v2, ICESA v2, XML v1; 2026 specifications) and Quarterly Wage Report Testing page
article_or_section: File Format Specifications; Record tables; Document Change Logs
figure_or_rule_carried: After MiUI launch, quarterly wage reports (current and past due) are submitted in MiUI in one of four formats: Delimited CSV (.txt/.csv), ICESA (NASWA, .txt), EFW2 (formerly MMREF-SSA, .txt, fixed 512-byte records, Employer Header RE + Employee Detail RS, many SSA fields Not Used by MI UIA), XML (.xml). Legacy MiWAM file format no longer accepted. Change logs: 2026 v1 2026-02-23; Delimited v2 2026-03-30 (EAN max length 10 -> 7), v3 2026-04-08 (blank/0 Obligation Gross Wages); EFW2 v2 2026-04-03 (blank Out of State Wages). Reporting unit 000 = main company. Wage Report Validator Tool for tests (no live PII).

instrument_name: Michigan Prevailing Wages on State Projects, 2023 PA 10 as amended by 2024 PA 110 (MCL 408.1101-408.1122): certified payroll and records
figure_or_rule_carried: Scope: state projects (construction etc. authorised by a public contracting agent and state-financed in whole or part) and, from 2025-04-02, private energy facility projects (solar/wind >= 2 MW, storage). No dollar threshold in the act. Contractors and subcontractors need a state project registration (sec. 2a, 2024 PA 110). Pay construction mechanics not less than locality prevailing wage and fringe rates; post rates on site; keep record of name, occupation, actual wages and benefits. Certified payroll records kept 3 years and transmitted within 10 days after the end of each pay period (to the contracting agent, then from 1 year after 2024 PA 110 to the LEO certified-payroll database): classification, apprentice/journeyman level, gross wages, hours per day, start/end times, hourly, overtime and fringe rates; no home address, phone or SSN in the database; e-signed attestation. Civil fine up to 5,000 per violation. Detail read on the local copy behind US-MIP51-006.

instrument_name: Office of Child Support Act, 1971 PA 174, sec. 6 (MCL 400.236) State Disbursement Unit
figure_or_rule_carried: The Michigan State Disbursement Unit (MiSDU) is the single location to which a payer or source of income (employer) sends withheld support and fee payments; SDU disburses within 2 business days; an NSF payment from the source of income can be collected with expenses. Employer fee for processing an IWO: not located in the sections read (open).

instrument_name: Michigan UIA Employer FAQ - Taxable Wage Base
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base 9,000 for qualified (non-delinquent) employers; delinquent employers do not qualify (9,500). Trigger: Trust Fund >= 2.5 billion on 30 June of the prior year and the next quarter. Page states a new employer at 2.7% saves on average 14.00 per employee: 0.027 x (9,500 - 9,000) = 13.50, rounded on the page to 14 (derivation reconciles the 9,000/9,500 pair with MCL 421.44(4), US-MIS5-010). Payroll systems must set the 2026 taxable wage at 9,000. No 2027 base stated.

instrument_name: MDHHS Office of Child Support - New Hire Reporting (employers)
authority: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services - Office of Child Support
article_or_section: superseded source copy (MDHHS Office of Child Support - New Hire Reporting (employers)): New Hire Reporting page
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers must report newly hired or rehired employees to the Office of Child Support through the Michigan New Hires Operation Center, (800) 524-9846, via the Michigan New Hire Reporting website (mi-newhire.com; Form 3281 per Treasury forms list). Page states no deadline, fields or penalty: deadline rests on federal 42 USC 653a 20 days (US-FED-017); Michigan statute not located. [SUPERSEDED 2026-11-02 by US-MIB5-001 (Synthesis D)]

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 177.24 Payment of minimum wages (Minnesota Fair Labor Standards Act)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage = rate set under subd. 1(c) from 2018-01-01; 90-day training wage for employees under 20 (subd. 1(b)). Indexation: by Aug 31 each year DLI determines the 12-month change in the PCE implicit price deflator (BEA); both rates rise by the lesser of 5% or that percentage, rounded to the nearest cent, never reduced, effective the next Jan 1. No tip credit: gratuities may not be applied to the minimum wage (subd. 2); tips are the employee's property, pooling only voluntary (subd. 3); card tips paid no later than the next scheduled pay period (subd. 3a). Uniform/equipment deductions capped at 50 USD and never below the minimum wage; reimbursed at termination (subd. 4-5). History ends 2024 c 110: no 2025/2026 amendment.

instrument_name: DLI page: Minimum wage in Minnesota (rates 2026 and 2027)
authority: Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage 11.41 USD/h from 2026-01-01 and 11.87 USD/h from 2027-01-01 (all employers); 90-day training wage (under 20) 9.31 from 2026-01-01 and 9.68 from 2027-01-01. 'No employer may take a tip credit against minimum wages in Minnesota.' Page points to the Minneapolis and St. Paul city minimum wages. Consistency check: 11.87/11.41 = 1.0403 and 9.68/9.31 = 1.0397, both under the 5% cap of 177.24 subd. 1(c); the PCE percentage itself was not read (DLI minimum-wage report not fetched).

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 177.25 Overtime
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime at 1.5x the regular rate for hours over 48 in a workweek (state rule; FLSA 40 hours governs FLSA-covered employers). Public employers may give comp time at 1.5 h per hour over 48. Health care facilities: 14-day period by prior agreement, overtime over 8 h/day and 80 h/14 days. Exemptions: commission auto/farm-implement sales and mechanics, on-farm silo piece rate, air carrier voluntary shift trades.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 177.23 subd. 7 Definition of employee (MFLSA exemptions)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: MFLSA 'employee' excludes: small salaried agricultural groups (2 or fewer salaried, or salary above 48 h at minimum + 17 h at 1.5x); certain minors in agriculture and corn detasselers (for 177.24); seasonal camp staff; bona fide executive/administrative/professional and outside salespeople (<=20% of sales on premises); volunteers for nonprofits; elected officials; political-subdivision police/fire; taxicab drivers; sole-practitioner babysitters; seasonal carnival/circus/fair/ski (for 177.25 overtime only); minors under 18 working under 20 h/week in municipal recreation; DOT-regulated drivers (49 USC 31502); seafarers; clergy and members of religious orders serving under religious obligations.
