instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 181.101 Wages; how often paid (as amended by Laws 2026 c 106 art 15 s 5)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: All wages (salary, earnings, gratuities) paid at least once every 31 days, commissions at least every 3 months, on a regular payday designated in advance; wages for the first half of the first 31-day period due on the first regular payday after the first day of work; wages are earned on the day worked; agricultural labor included. DLI demand: if unpaid 10 days after demand, penalty = average daily earnings per day. (b) paid on-call firefighters, first responders, volunteer ambulance: every 31 days unless mutually agreed longer. Last amended 2026 c 106 art 15 s 5 (firefighter wording only, see US-MNS5-022).

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 181.13 Penalty for failure to pay wages promptly (discharge)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Discharge: earned and unpaid wages and commissions immediately due on the employee's written demand; default if not paid within 24 hours after demand; penalty = average daily earnings for each day up to 15 days. Public employer needing board approval: the 24 h run from the first board meeting after discharge. Paid in the usual manner unless the employee asks for mail (postmark date = payment date).

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 181.14 Payment to employees who quit or resign
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Resignation: wages and commissions paid in full no later than the first regularly scheduled payday after the final day (unless a CBA differs); if that payday is less than 5 calendar days after the final day, may wait until the second regular payday but no later than 20 calendar days after the final day. Migrant workers: within 3 days. Late: payable on written demand, penalty average daily earnings up to 15 days. Employees entrusted with money/property: employer has 10 calendar days to audit. No deduction for loss/indebtedness except as 181.79 permits.

instrument_name: Minneapolis Minimum Wage (City of Minneapolis Labor Standards site)
authority: City of Minneapolis, Labor Standards Enforcement Division
figure_or_rule_carried: Minneapolis minimum wage 16.37 USD/h for work performed in Minneapolis during 2026; 17.02 USD/h from 2027-01-01; same rate regardless of employer size or employee age; indexed every January 1 for inflation, capped at 5%.

instrument_name: Saint Paul Minimum Wage Ordinance rates (city HREEO Labor Standards page)
authority: City of Saint Paul, Department of Human Rights and Equal Economic Opportunity, Labor Standards
figure_or_rule_carried: Macro (10,001+ employees) and City of Saint Paul: 16.37 from 2026-01-01; Large (101-10,000): 16.37 from 2026-01-01; Small (6-100): 15.00 from 2025-07-01, 16.37 from 2026-07-01; Micro (5 or fewer): 13.25 from 2025-07-01, 14.25 from 2026-07-01, 15.00 from 2027-07-01, city indexed rate from 2028-07-01; youth/training wage 12.75 from 2025-07-01, 13.95 from 2026-07-01. Macro/Large from 2027-01-01 and Small from 2027-07-01: 'City Rate' = inflation-indexed (figure not on the page). City minimum applies from the 18th birthday even within the first 90 days. Ordinance text on Municode not fetched.

instrument_name: Minnesota Income Tax Withholding Instruction Booklet and Tax Tables 2026 (wh-inst-26): computer formula, deposits, returns, W-2
figure_or_rule_carried: Formula (supersedes formulas before 2026-01-01): annualise wages (x360/52/26/24/12/1), minus allowances x 5,300. Single: 4,700-38,010 at 5.35% of excess over 4,700; 38,010-114,130 = 1,782.09 + 6.80% over 38,010; 114,130-207,850 = 6,958.25 + 7.85% over 114,130; over 207,850 = 14,315.27 + 9.85% over 207,850. Married: 14,700-63,400 at 5.35% over 14,700; 63,400-208,180 = 2,605.45 + 6.80%; 208,180-352,630 = 12,450.49 + 7.85%; over 352,630 = 23,789.82 + 9.85%. Divide by periods; 'You may round the amount to the nearest dollar'. No W-4MN = single, zero allowances; W-4MN copies to DOR if >10 allowances or exempt box with wages >200/week; exempt claim renewed yearly. Supplemental 6.25% (Method 1 aggregate / Method 2 flat). Backup withholding 9.85%. Nonresidents: no MN withholding if expected pay < 15,300 or MI/ND reciprocity with MWR. Deposits on the federal semiweekly/monthly schedule (monthly by the 15th), MN did not adopt the one-day rule; quarterly returns Apr 30/Jul 31/Oct 31/Jan 31, filed electronically; annual filers (<=500 prior year) Jan 31. W-2 to employees and W-2 information to DOR by Jan 31; e-Services mandatory if more than 10 W-2 + 1099. Withholding definitions follow the IRC as amended through 2023-05-01; MN has not adopted the H.R. 1 (2025) withholding changes. 2026 interest rate 7%.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 181.9445-181.9448 Earned Sick and Safe Time (ESST)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer = 1+ employees; employee = anticipated to work 80+ hours/year in MN (temporary and part-time included). Accrual 1 hour per 30 hours worked, max 48 hours/year unless the employer agrees more; carryover with an 80-hour balance cap, or front-load 48 h (if unused hours are paid out at year end) / 80 h (if not paid out); FLSA 213(a)(1) exempt employees deemed to work 40 h/week; accrual from hire; use as accrued, increments not below 15 min nor required above 4 h. At the end of each pay period the employer must provide, in writing or electronically, the ESST hours available and the hours used in the period (on or attached to the earnings statement or via an electronic system). No payout at separation required (181.9448 subd. 2). Benefits maintained; return at the same rate. Last amended 1Sp2025 c 6 art 5.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 181.79 (deductions for loss/indebtedness) and 181.06 (assignment of wages; payroll deductions)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: No deduction for lost/stolen property, damage or any employee debt unless the employee authorises it in writing after the loss/debt arises (amount per pay period stated) or a court holds the employee liable; never above the garnishment-exempt limit; exceptions: CBA, commissioned-salespeople rules, prior written authorisation for a purchase/loan from the employer. Violation: liable for twice the deduction. 181.06: assignment of wages earned more than 60 days ahead void (except above the first 1,500/month for less than 5 years); a written contract may authorise deductions for union dues, insurance premiums, credit unions, charities, PACs, ESPP/savings plans and similar.
verification_method: inspected directly | effective_from not stated in the instrument; in force as at retrieved_on 2026-11-02 (QA r3b fix: row newly recorded as CCG-consumed)

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 571.922 Limitation on wage garnishment
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Non-support garnishment: the lesser of the tiered percentage of disposable earnings (25% if weekly income > 80x the hourly minimum; 15% if > 60x and <= 80x; 10% if > 40x and <= 60x) or the excess of disposable earnings over 40x the greater of the state minimum wage (177.24 subd. 1(a)(4)) or the federal minimum, per work week in the pay period. Child-support judgments: 50%/55% (supporting a spouse/child, judgment <=12 / >12 weeks old) or 60%/65% (not supporting). Stricter than CCPA 25%. Last amended 1Sp2025 c 4 art 7 s 34.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 518A.53 Income withholding (child support)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Payor remits withheld support to the public authority within 7 business days of the payday, with the obligor's SSN; no discharge/discipline because of withholding; multiple orders honoured within CCPA 15 USC 1673(b) limits with priority to current support; termination of employment notified to the public authority within 10 days (home address, new payor if known). Support withholding has priority over any other attachment, execution, garnishment or wage assignment (subd. 9), which lists the employer's fee for processing a withholding notice; the fee amount was not located in the text read. Income-withholding-only service fee 15 USD/month charged to the obligor.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 268.044 Wage reporting (UI quarterly wage detail report)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly wage detail report by electronic transmission in the commissioner's format: per employee name, SSN, total wages and total paid hours worked (exempt full-time employees: 40 h per week with duties; reasonable estimate otherwise); wages may be reported to the next lower whole dollar; a report is required each quarter even with no wages until termination of business is notified. Late fee 10 USD per employee (minimum 250), doubled if not filed 30 days after demand; missing/erroneous data 25 USD per employee; omitted employee 2% of that employee's wages. Quarterly due date not stated in this section. | Subd. 1(a) (held copy re-read 2026-11-03): 'The report is due and must be received by the commissioner on or before the last day of the month following the end of the calendar quarter'; the commissioner may delay the due date for a quarter when the department cannot accept reports electronically; report also carries employees in the payroll period including the 12th of each month, by business location if required.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 142A.29 Work reporting system (new-hire reporting; renumbered from 256.998)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Report each new hire or rehire (return after 60+ days' separation) of an employee who resides or works in MN, within 20 calendar days of the date of hiring, to the Commissioner of Children, Youth, and Families; not required if employed less than 2 months and gross under 250 USD/month; contents = federal requirements; means: copy of W-4/W-9, electronic media or other authorised means; domestic service in a private home excluded from 'employee'; the state and political subdivisions must also report independent contractors, other payors may. Penalty 25 USD per intentionally unreported employee after a notice of noncompliance.
verification_method: inspected directly | effective_from not stated in the instrument; in force as at retrieved_on (QA r1 note)

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 268.035 subd. 20 (noncovered employment) and subd. 24 (taxable wages)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wages = wages in covered employment per calendar year up to 60% of the state's average annual wage, rounded to the nearest 1,000 (2026 figure 44,000 in US-MNP52-001). Not covered: churches, church-controlled religious nonprofits and church schools; ministers and members of religious orders; domestic employment if quarterly domestic wages were under 1,000 in the current and prior year; employment by a son/daughter/spouse and of a child under 18 by a parent; students employed by their school; full-time students in credit programmes; J-1 summer work travel; Minneapolis/St. Paul student interns; student nurses; casual non-business employment; agricultural employment unless 'covered agricultural employment' (subd. 11, not read); H-2A workers. Read literally; replaces the summarizer reading in US-MNP51-003.
verification_method: inspected directly | effective_from not stated in the instrument; in force as at retrieved_on (QA r2 note)

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 268B.14 Paid Leave premiums (statute text)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Payments by electronic payment (also third-party processors). Employer pays at least 50% of the premium; the employee share is a wage deduction in equal proportion to wages and may not reduce pay below the minimum wage. Wage cap = maximum earnings subject to OASDI in the year. Statutory base rates from 2026-01-01: 0.7% (family + medical), 0.4% (medical only, private family plan), 0.3% (family only, private medical plan); the commissioner may adjust before 2026-01-01 and must adjust by July 31 each year for the following year (projected fund balance >= 25%). The adjusted rate in force (0.88% for 2026 and 2027) is on the DEED page, US-MNP52-003. History ends 1Sp2025 c 6 art 4 s 27. Replaces the summarizer reading US-MNP51-002.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 325E.59 Use of Social Security numbers
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Private persons may not publicly display an SSN, require its transmission over the Internet unless secure/encrypted, require it to access a website without a password, or print it on materials mailed to the individual unless state or federal law requires it (mailed applications/forms allowed); exceptions for uses required/authorised by law and internal verification/administrative use. No statutory SSN-truncation rule for pay statements located (the 181.032 content list does not require the SSN).

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 177.30 Keeping records (MFLSA)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Payroll records kept for three years in the premises where the employee works; employers on state-funded public works projects keep them three years after the project (177.41-177.44).

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 268.068 Notice to workers (UI)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Posting duty only: the employer posts the DEED-supplied statement of the right to apply for unemployment benefits. No individual UI separation notice in statute (the 2020 executive-order notice expired 2020-12-31; tier-B lead only).

instrument_name: Laws 2026, chapter 106 (H.F. 4074), article 15 (retirement omnibus; firefighter conforming changes)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes

Guide example (married spouse works, 35,000) = 707.81/yr, 59/month - re-derived. MO W-4 (filing status, Line 2 additional, Line 3 fixed amount); no MO W-4 = single. Annual: W-2 + MO W-3 by last day of January (electronic) / end of February (paper); 250+ W-2s must file electronically in EFW2 incl. RV record. Timely compensation deduction 2%/1%/0.5% (YTD 0-5,000 / 5,001-10,000 / >10,000). Interest 7% for 2026. No reciprocity with any state; MO W-4A nonresident percentage; MO W-4C difference withholding

instrument_name: RSMo 290.110 Payment due discharged employee - penalty for delay
figure_or_rule_carried: On discharge or refusal to further employ: unpaid wages due on the day of discharge; employee may request in writing that pay be sent; if not received within 7 days of the request, wages continue as penalty at the same rate until paid, max 60 days. Exception: primarily-commission employees whose net pay needs an audit. No resignation-timing rule in this section.

instrument_name: RSMo 290.512 Tipped employees and goods/services as wages
figure_or_rule_carried: Tipped employees: employer pays not less than 50% of the state minimum wage (2026: 7.50/h = 15.00 x 0.5, derived), total compensation must reach the minimum wage, employer makes up the difference. Goods/services as incident of employment: fair market value credit computed weekly.

instrument_name: RSMo 290.500 Definitions (minimum wage law exclusions)
figure_or_rule_carried: Excluded from 'employee': bona fide executive/administrative/professional; volunteers; occasional private-residence work <=6h per occasion; casual babysitting; retail/service business with annual gross volume < 500,000; government positions per 29 USC 203(e)(2)(C); 29 USC 213(a)(8); uncontrolled commission salespersons; caddies/newsboys; tuition-offset student workers; offenders. Learner/apprentice = under 20, max 3 (6) months.

instrument_name: RSMo 525.030 Wage garnishment limits
figure_or_rule_carried: Max garnishable per workweek (after legally required deductions) = least of 25%, excess over 30x federal minimum wage, or 10% if the employee is head of a family and a Missouri resident. Limits do not apply to support orders, Chapter XIII bankruptcy orders, state/federal tax debts. Longer periods: month = 4 1/3 weeks, semimonthly = 2 1/6 weeks. No discharge for garnishment for any one indebtedness.

instrument_name: RSMo 285.304 Content of new-hire withholding forms

instrument_name: RSMo 290.140 Service letter on request
figure_or_rule_carried: Corporations with 7+ employees: an employee with 90+ days of service who is discharged or quits and requests in writing by certified mail within 1 year gets, within 45 days, a signed letter stating the nature and duration of service and the true cause of separation.

instrument_name: RSMo 288.036 Wages defined - state taxable wage base mechanism
figure_or_rule_carried: UI wages include commissions, bonuses, non-cash remuneration, FUTA-reportable tips; exclude sickness/accident/medical/death plan payments, 401(a) trust and 404(a)(2) annuity payments, employer-paid FICA for domestic/agricultural service, Section 125 cafeteria payments that are not FUTA wages; domestic and agricultural: cash wages only. Wage base set annually from the 4-quarter average trust fund balance: <=350M -> +1,000; >=650M -> -500; floor 7,000, cap 13,000 (from 2010). G-DERIVE: 2025 9,500 -> 2026 9,000 = -500 step, consistent with the >=650M branch and with DES page US-MOP52-005. instrument_name: Missouri DES Employers Rights and Responsibilities under the Missouri Employment Security Law (MODES-INF-151 (10-25) AI)
authority: Missouri Department of Labor and Industrial Relations, Division of Employment Security
article_or_section: pp.5, 13-15, 17, 22 (liability, wages, taxable wage base, contribution and wage report, online reporting, localization, posters)
figure_or_rule_carried: Liability: 1,500 payroll in a quarter or a worker in 20 weeks; domestic 1,000 cash in a quarter; agricultural 10+ workers in 20 weeks or 20,000 cash in a quarter; government any worker. Taxable wage limitations 2022 11,000 / 2023 10,500 / 2024 10,000 / 2025 9,500 / 2026 9,000 (+1,000 / -500 steps; 7,000-13,000). Quarterly Contribution and Wage Report (MODES-4; instructions MODES-4-5): worker name, SSN, wages paid in the quarter, work-separation dates and probationary dates (<=28 days, flag P); due last day of the month after quarter end (Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31); online via UInteract (Method B file upload; payroll services NASWA/ICESA format); employers filing W-2 electronically with SSA (50+ employees) must report quarterly wages electronically; spec labor.mo.gov/media/pdf/m-inf-368-ai. Late penalty 10% of tax or 100, whichever greater. No part of the tax may be deducted from pay. Localization: localized / base of operations / direction and control / residence; Interstate Reciprocal Coverage election. Poster MODES-B-2 required. 401(k) elective deferrals are UI wages.

instrument_name: RSMo 454.505 Administrative income withholding for support

instrument_name: RSMo 143.011 Resident individuals - tax rates - rate reductions - bracket indexation
figure_or_rule_carried: Base table 1.5% to 6% in 1,000 steps; top rate 4.95% from 2023 (subs. 2), top rate applies above 7,000 as adjusted; subs. 3: one 0.15-point cut from 2024 if net general revenue exceeds the best of the prior 3 years by 175M; subs. 4: up to three further 0.1-point cuts, one per year, if revenue triggers (200M, inflation-adjusted) are met; bracket eliminated once top rate falls below it; subs. 5: brackets indexed annually by CPI-U (Sep-Aug average vs Sep 2014-Aug 2015), published by DOR from Oct 1. G-DERIVE: 4.95 - 0.15 - 0.10 = 4.70 = the 2026 top/supplemental rate in Form 4282 (US-MOS5-001), so one subs. 4 cut has been applied and two remain possible (4.6, 4.5). 2026 bracket width 1,348 = 1,000 x indexation factor 1.348 (DOR figure). Wayback snapshot 2026-08-03 predates the 2026-08-28 effective date of 2026-session acts: a 2026 amendment cannot be excluded from this read.

instrument_name: RSMo 407.1500 Breach of security - notice to consumers

Breach notice to affected Missouri residents without unreasonable delay; notice to the Attorney General and nationwide consumer reporting agencies when more than 1,000 residents are notified; Attorney General exclusive action, civil penalty up to 150,000 per breach.

Standard deduction: single 2,300; HoF 3,400; married 4,600 (both employed 2,300 each). Tax year 2026: 0% on first 10,000 taxable income, 4.0% above. Monthly/quarterly returns due 15th of following month (DOR sets frequency); TAP e-file mandatory at 10+ W-2s/1099s; W-2 EFW2 RS record due Jan 31; Form 89-140 with paper filers (<10); W-2 to terminated employee within 30 days; records 3 years; penalty 10%; interest per month on delinquent tax.

instrument_name: MDOR Business Tax Frequently Asked Questions - Withholding Tax section
article_or_section: Withholding Tax; Filing Withholding Returns; Registration and Updating Account Information
figure_or_rule_carried: Employee refusing Form 89-350: withhold as single, no exemptions. Employer must send DOR a copy of any certificate claiming more than 10 allowances or 'exempt' where wages normally exceed 200 USD/week. MS resident working in another state with an income tax: employer withholds for the other state, not MS (credit at assessment). Nonresident working in MS: withhold on MS-service wages unless MS earnings for the year will be less than the standard deduction for the filing status. Withheld in wrong state: reimburse employee and amend. Reservation Indian living and working on reservation exempt with Form 80-340. Pensions/annuities not subject to MS withholding. Domestic help in the home exempt. Section 125 pre-tax. Corporate officers = employees. Severance taxable. Bonus with regular wages: aggregate. Tips paid directly by customers not subject to withholding (still taxable); tips paid through employer subject. Family members including children under 18 subject. Returns due 15th; monthly if average liability >= 300 USD/month, else quarterly; no depository system (pay with return); e-file and e-pay mandatory if liability >= 20,000 USD in any period; late payment penalty 10% + interest 1/2% per month; W-2C copy to DOR if MS wages/withholding change; no W-2 filing extensions; records 3 years (payroll, employee list, salaries, SSNs, addresses). Registration via TAP: required for employers doing business in MS, paying MS residents anywhere, or paying nonresidents for MS services; 8-digit MS account number (not FEIN); new account if FEIN changes or business purchased. 1099/info returns: report personal-service income over 3,000 USD.

instrument_name: Ward v. United Airlines, Inc. (Cal. Supreme Court, S248702, 2020-06-29), 9 Cal.5th 732: geographic reach of Labor Code 226
article_or_section: Part III; Part IV answers (1)-(2); Lab. Code 226; Wage Order 9 sec.1(E)
figure_or_rule_carried: STATUS: in force (final answer to Ninth Circuit certified question). LEVEL: employer pay-statement duty (payroll output), not tax. Rule: Lab. Code 226 (CA itemized wage statement) applies if the employee's PRINCIPAL PLACE OF WORK is in California: works the majority of the time in CA; for interstate transportation workers and others not working a majority anywhere, CA is their base of work operations (e.g. home-base airport) plus some work in CA. Employer location, employee residence, place of pay receipt and payment of taxes are NOT pertinent; a CBA does not oust 226.

instrument_name: Oman v. Delta Air Lines, Inc. (Cal. Supreme Court, S248726, 2020-06-29), 9 Cal.5th 762: reach of Lab. Code 204 and 226 to multistate workers; Sullivan v. Oracle (2011) 51 Cal.4th 1191 as cited
figure_or_rule_carried: STATUS: in force. LEVEL: employer pay timing and pay statement. (1) Lab. Code 204 (pay-day timing) and 226 do not apply to pay periods in which the employee works in CA only episodically and for less than a day at a time, unless the employee works primarily in CA during the pay period or works primarily in no State and has the base of operations in CA. Application of CA wage-hour law to multistate workers varies statute by statute (Sullivan v. Oracle Corp. (2011) 51 Cal.4th 1191, 1201); employer's nonresident domicile does not exempt it. (3) Geographic reach of the CA minimum wage law left undecided.

instrument_name: Illinois DOR Publication 130 (R-02/26) Who is Required to Withhold Illinois Income Tax: 'When is compensation paid in Illinois' (localization rules 1-4, 30-working-day rule)
article_or_section: pp.3-5 When is compensation paid in Illinois, rules 1-4; examples
figure_or_rule_carried: Illinois sources wage withholding by UI-style LOCALIZATION: (1) all service in IL; (2) out-of-IL service only incidental (temporary, transitory, isolated); (3) IL resident and no rule applies and no other State's tax withheld; (4) service not localized anywhere: withhold on the IL fraction (IL working days / total working days) only if the employee performs significant, nonincidental service in IL on MORE THAN 30 working days. A working day is in IL if more duty time is spent in IL that day (travel excluded) or the only duty is travel arriving in IL; disaster-response days excluded. Example: 35 of 250 days = 14%. Reciprocity carve-out: IA, KY, MI, WI residents and military spouses. Adds the threshold that US-ILP51-001 (same publication) does not carry.

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.1 Wage and Hour Act - local governments preempted
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: State Wage and Hour Act supersedes and preempts any local ordinance imposing requirements on employers on compensation, wage levels, hours, payment of earned wages, benefits, leave or well-being of minors (S.L. 2023-134 s.5.9(a)); exceptions only for a local government's own employees, economic-development incentives, CDBG, G.S. 160D-1311 programs. instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.3 Minimum wage
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage = higher of 6.15 USD/h or the FLSA 29 USC 206(a)(1) rate as it changes (federal 7.25 USD/h, see FED unit) -> 7.25 USD/h in 2026; no state indexation. Full-time students, learners, apprentices, messengers: 90% of the (a) rate rounded to the lowest nickel (7.25 x 0.9 = 6.525 -> 6.50 USD/h, derived). Tip credit only up to the FLSA 3(m) amount, with advance notice, retention of all tips and monthly/per-period tip certification; tip pool may not reduce an employee's tips by more than 15%.

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.7 Payment to separated employees
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Separated employees (any reason: discharge and resignation alike) paid all wages due on or before the next regular payday, through regular pay channels or by trackable mail if the employee requests in writing; bonuses/commissions paid on the first regular payday after the amount becomes calculable; forfeiture only if notified per G.S. 95-25.13.

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.8 Withholding of wages (deduction authorization)
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Deductions allowed when required by law, or with signed written authorization stating reason and amount/percentage (known amount) or reason plus advance written notice of actual amount and right to withdraw (unknown amount). Deductions for the employer's benefit may reduce pay only to minimum wage and never overtime wages; cash/inventory shortage or property damage needs 7 days' written notice (not at separation). Overpayments by bona fide error, wage advances and loan principal are prepayment of wages and deductible. Authorization/notice may be electronic (UETA).

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.12 Vacation pay plans
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: No duty to provide vacation; if provided, time off or payment in lieu per company policy/practice; forfeiture of accrued vacation (incl. at separation) only if the employee was notified of the forfeiture policy per G.S. 95-25.13 (13 NCAC 12 .0805(c): unwritten forfeiture policy unenforceable).

instrument_name: G.S. 95-25.14 Exemptions from minimum wage, overtime, youth employment
authority: NC General Assembly (General Statutes, official host ncleg.gov)

Exempt from OT only: drivers/loaders/mechanics, taxi drivers, seamen/rail/air, auto/truck/farm-implement dealer salespersons and mechanics, live-in child-care workers, seasonal amusement. State and local government: only minimum wage, definitions, exemptions and complainant protection apply.

instrument_name: NH Lab 800 rules (Lab 803.01 payment of wages, 803.03 notification and records, 803.05 exemptions)
authority: NH Department of Labor / Office of Legislative Services
figure_or_rule_carried: Biweekly pay: first payment within 8 days (incl. Sunday) after the work weeks; petition for semi-monthly/monthly pay lists 7 data items and is granted case by case. instrument_name: NH RSA 282-A:117-a Employment Reports to NHES; State Directory of New Hires
figure_or_rule_carried: New-hire report to NHES within 20 days of hire or rehire (electronic filers: 2 monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart); also independent contractors (non-casual) when payment is expected to exceed USD 2,500. Content: full name, address, SSN, first day of work; employer name, address, federal and state ID. W-4 copy acceptable. Multistate employers may designate one state (notify HHS).

instrument_name: NH RSA chapter 282-A Unemployment Compensation: 282-A:9 (employment, localization, exclusions), 282-A:15 (wages), 282-A:69 (payment of contributions)
figure_or_rule_carried: 282-A:69 I: contributions 2.7% (subject to experience rating RSA 282-A:79-90) on wages up to USD 14,000 per individual per calendar year; contributions shall NOT be deducted in whole or part from employee wages (no employee share); for the 14,000 base, wages include service subject to another state's employment security law (credit for wages reported to another state). Base is a fixed statutory figure, not indexed. 282-A:9 I: localization test (localized / base of operations / direction and control). Exclusions incl. domestic service unless cash >= USD 1,000 in a quarter; services of minister/religious order; students employed by their school; individual employed by son/daughter/spouse and child under 21 employed by parent; agricultural labor covered per FUTA 3306(c)(1). 282-A:15: wages include bonuses, board, lodging, payment in kind; exclude employer payments under a plan for retirement, third-party sickness/disability, medical/hospitalization, SUB, death benefits, employer-paid FICA. No express exclusion for employee elective deferrals (401(k)/125) located in 282-A:15.

instrument_name: NH RSA chapter 458-B Income Assignment (child/spousal support)
figure_or_rule_carried: Arrearage add-on at least 20% of current support; lump-sum payments (severance, accumulated sick/vacation pay, bonuses, commissions) subject to assignment up to arrearage when obligor non-compliant; total withheld capped at 15 U.S.C. 1673(b). Priority: current support, health insurance/cash medical, arrears, other. Employer: implement no later than the first pay period occurring 14 days after notice mailed; remit at the same time the obligor is paid; support withholding has priority over other state legal process; employer may deduct a fee of USD 1.00 per withholding; notify within 15 days of termination with last known address and new employer; administrative fine USD 100 per pay period per employee for willful failure; discharge/discipline for withholding = misdemeanor, fine up to USD 1,000.

instrument_name: NH RSA 512:21 List of Exemptions (trustee process / wage garnishment for creditor debts)
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages for labor performed after service of the writ are exempt (I). Wages earned before service are exempt except in actions on a debt on a New Hampshire court judgment; then 50 x the FLSA minimum hourly wage per week is exempt (50 x 7.25 = USD 362.50/week) and paid on the usual payday (II). Loan contracts under RSA 399-A: USD 50/week exempt (IX). More protective than CCPA 30x. Payroll accounts exempt (XI).

instrument_name: NH RSA chapter 359-C Right to Privacy: 359-C:19-21 security breach notification
figure_or_rule_carried: Personal information = name + SSN, driver's licence/government ID, or financial account number with access code (unencrypted). Breach of computerized data: notify affected individuals as soon as possible when misuse occurred or is reasonably likely; notify the NH Attorney General (or primary regulator) with anticipated notice date and approximate number of NH individuals; data maintainers (e.g. payroll processors) notify the owner immediately. No pay-statement SSN-truncation rule found in this chapter.

instrument_name: NH RSA chapter 275 Protective Legislation (consolidated chapter, Wayback 2026-03-19): 275:30-a, 275:37-d, 275:43-a, 275:43-c, 275:47, 275:57, 275:78-83
figure_or_rule_carried: 30-minute meal period after 5 consecutive hours (unless eating while working is permitted). Reporting pay: minimum 2 hours at regular rate when employee reports at employer's request (not counties/municipalities). 275:37-d: employers with 50+ employees sponsoring Granite State FML insurance must restore the employee and continue health insurance (eff 2021-07-01, am. 2023). 275:43-c: small employers (2+ NH employees, no employer health plan) may set up a premium-only section 125 plan; employees working >15 h/week may buy small-group coverage by payroll deduction. instrument_name: NHES Employer Handbook NHES 0041 R-8/16 (listed by NHES as current Employer Handbook on 2026-10-30): taxes, new hire, mass layoff, posting chapters
article_or_section: Handbook pp. 6-10, 14; attachments IV, V, VII, VIII

Employer must give partially employed claimants proof of earnings. Highest earned rate 7.0%. Procedural/2016 edition: fee and interest figures to be re-verified against RSA 282-A:? or Emp 300 rules.

instrument_name: NH RSA chapter 276-A Youth Employment
figure_or_rule_carried: Under 16: certificate required (except work for parents/grandparents/guardian, casual work, farm labor); hours 7 a.m.-9 p.m., max 3 h on school days and 23 h in school weeks, 8 h on non-school days, 48 h/week in vacations. Under 12: only family, casual or newspaper delivery. 16-17 enrolled in school: max 35 h in a 5-day school week; max 6 consecutive days / 48 h per week in vacations (summer = June 1 to Labor Day; camp exception). 16-17 without diploma/GED: signed parental permission kept on file. No youth in hazardous occupations except approved programmes. (Pay impact: minimum wage for 16 and under is 75% of the statutory minimum per RSA 279:21 V, register US-NHS5-003.)

instrument_name: NH RSA 21-I:103 Granite State Paid Family Leave Plan: coverage for other employers and individual employees
figure_or_rule_carried: Voluntary FMLI (no mandatory payroll levy): private employers with more than 50 employees may sponsor coverage by contracting directly with the state's carrier; contributory, partially contributory or non-contributory plans and payroll deduction/premium remittance procedures set by the commissioner. Employees of non-sponsoring employers may buy individual coverage through the NHES-administered purchasing pool (RSA 282-B): 7-month waiting period, 1-week elimination period, 60-day open enrollment; premium capped at USD 5 per subscriber per week. Payroll impact only where the employer sponsors a contributory plan (voluntary post-tax/agreed deduction under RSA 275:48).

instrument_name: NH DRA: Granite State Paid Family and Medical Leave Plan Tax Credit (RSA 77-E:3-e)
figure_or_rule_carried: Business Enterprise Tax credit = 50% of the premium paid by a sponsoring employer for FMLI coverage under RSA 21-I:103, for the taxable period in which paid. Entity-level BET item, not a payroll calculation (BET excluded from payroll scope per US-OWN-007).

instrument_name: N.J.S.A. 34:11-4.2 Time and mode of payment; paydays (Wage Payment Law), as reprinted by NJDOL
authority: NJ Legislature (text as published by NJ DOL Wage and Hour Compliance, Selected NJ State Labor Laws)
figure_or_rule_carried: Pay full wages at least twice each calendar month on regular paydays designated in advance; bona fide executive/supervisory/special classes (reg: overtime-exempt under N.J.A.C. 12:56-7) may be paid less often but at least once a month. Payday on a nonwork day -> preceding work day (unless CBA). Pay period must end not more than 10 working days before the payday. Payment in US money or checks cashable without difficulty; employer bears check-cashing fee at the drawee bank and check-deposit-return fees (12:55-2.4(e)-(g)).

instrument_name: N.J.S.A. 34:11-4.3 Termination or suspension of employment; N.J.A.C. 12:55-2.4(a)-(c)
authority: NJ Legislature / NJ DOL (text as published by NJ DOL)
figure_or_rule_carried: Discharge, layoff, suspension or quit for any reason: all wages due not later than the regular payday for the pay period in which employment ended (incentive pay: reasonable approximation until computed); labor-dispute suspension involving payroll staff: +10 days. Paid through regular channels or by mail if the employee requests. Regulation 12:55-2.4(a) words it as final payment within 10 days from the end of the work period, in compliance with 34:11-4.2. Same rule for discharge and resignation. Accrued vacation: no statutory payout; the Wage Payment Law enforces only the benefits the employer agreed to provide (NJ DOL Wage Payment page, 'Fringe Benefits').

instrument_name: NJDOL Earned Sick Leave: What Employers Need to Know (MW-566, 12/23) - N.J.S.A. 34:11D-1 et seq.
authority: NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development
figure_or_rule_carried: All employers, all sizes; full/part-time, temporary, seasonal. Exempt: union construction workers, per diem health care, public employees with full-pay sick leave under other law. Accrual 1 hour per 30 hours worked up to 40 hours per benefit year, or front-load at least 40 hours (may prorate new hires). Usable from day 120 of employment. Employer-fixed 12-month benefit year (30 days notice to NJDOL to change). Paid at the normal rate and at least the State minimum wage, in the same or next pay period. Unused: carry over (use capped at 40 h/yr) or pay out at end of benefit year. Documentation after 3+ consecutive days. Records 5 years. Notice in the employee's primary language if NJDOL publishes it.

article_or_section: Minimum Wage; Overtime; Payroll Deductions; Frequency of Payment; Benefits; Minors
figure_or_rule_carried: Banner: from 2027-01-01 minimum wage 16.48 USD/h for most workers. Overtime 1.5x regular rate for hours actually worked over 40 in a 7-day workweek (no daily overtime; no holiday/weekend premium; paid holiday hours do not count; not waivable); multiple rates -> weighted average, half-time premium. Exempt from minimum wage: automobile salespersons, outside salespersons, minors under 18 except in listed industries (retail, food service, first processing of farm products, beauty culture, laundry/cleaning/dyeing, light manufacturing/apparel, hotel/motel). Pay-statement content per FAQ: gross, net and itemized deductions, electronic or paper. Fringe benefits (vacation, severance, holiday) not required by NJ law; if provided, administered per policy. Minors under 18: 30-minute meal period after 5 consecutive hours; working papers for all under 18. 6-year statute of limitations on wage complaints. Jury duty: unpaid time off required.

instrument_name: Oregon DOR 150-206-436 Withholding Tax Formulas, effective 2026-01-01 (Rev. 12-31-25): annual brackets
figure_or_rule_carried: Annual formula. BASE = wages - federal tax withheld (cap 8,750; phase-out S: 125k-145k in 5k steps 7,000/5,250/3,500/1,750/0; M: 250k-290k in 10k steps) - standard deduction (2,910 single/HoH-claim or single <3 allowances; 5,820 married or single 3+ allowances). Wages <50,000, single: 0-4,550 WH = 263 + BASE x 0.0475; 4,550-11,400 WH = 479 + (BASE-4,550) x 0.0675; 11,400-50,000 WH = 941 + (BASE-11,400) x 0.0875. Married: 0-9,100 WH = 263 + BASE x 0.0475; 9,100-22,800 WH = 695 + (BASE-9,100) x 0.0675; 22,800-50,000 WH = 1,620 + (BASE-22,800) x 0.0875. Wages >=50,000, single: up to 125,000 WH = 678 + (BASE-11,400) x 0.0875; over 125,000 WH = 10,618 + (BASE-125,000) x 0.099. Married: up to 250,000 WH = 1,357 + (BASE-22,800) x 0.0875; over 250,000 WH = 21,237 + (BASE-250,000) x 0.099. Minus 263 per allowance (allowances = 0 if single >100,000 or married >200,000). Negative = 0. Divide annual by 12/24/26/52/260. Own formula needs DOR approval. Supplemental 8% flat optional; 8% default with no OR-W-4; exemption expires Feb 15. Rounding to dollar permitted. Text inconsistencies: federal cap stated 8,500 (p.5, FAQ 3, labelled 2025) vs 8,750 (pp.6-7, FAQ 11); Example 1 base 21,165 vs 21,090.

instrument_name: ORS chapter 316 (2025 Edition): 316.037 rates, 316.048 federal taxable income base, 316.162 wages definition, 316.167 withholding duty

Employer may elect 2% flat withholding for seasonal agricultural crop workers (316.167(1)).

LST (Sec. 301.1): maximum 52 USD per person per calendar year irrespective of number of jurisdictions; levies >10 USD collected pro rata per payroll period (annual rate / employer's number of payroll periods, rounded DOWN to the cent); levies >10 USD must exempt persons with earned income + net profits in the subdivision < 12,000 USD (optional for <=10 USD levies); mandatory exemptions for 100% disabled veterans and reservists called to active duty; situs = place of employment on first day of each payroll period (>10 USD) or of the year (<=10 USD); one subdivision per payroll period with priority principal office -> residence-and-work -> nearest to home; concurrent employment: non-principal employer refrains on a recent principal-employer pay statement plus employee statement. Sec. 312: LST remitted 30 days after end of each quarter.

figure_or_rule_carried: 9I-14: withhold on all wages of nonresidents for services in Utah and of residents for all services wherever performed; resident working in another state that requires withholding: Utah withholding = Utah tax less the other state's required withholding; nonresident working in and out of Utah: withhold on the portion allocable to Utah; rail/motor carrier employees under 49 USC 14503; withholding applies to all wages subject to federal income-tax withholding, employees per IRS guidelines; exemptions claimed for federal = state; use Tax Commission schedules/tables. 9I-15: no withholding from employee who filed federal W-4E (no-liability). 9I-16: W-2 must show names/addresses, Utah withholding account number, compensation, federal and Utah tax withheld, SSN, the word 'Utah'. 9I-17: quarterly default; annual filing/payment allowed for employers filing federal Schedule H or Form 944 (due 31 Jan); employers averaging 1,000 USD or more per month withholding prepay monthly. instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-28.10 Minimum wages (Virginia Minimum Wage Act)
authority: Virginia General Assembly (Code of Virginia, law.lis.virginia.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage greater of state rate or federal: 12.77 USD/h 2026-01-01 to 2027-01-01; 13.75 USD/h 2027-01-01 to 2028-01-01; 15.00 USD/h 2028-01-01 to 2029-01-01; from 2029-01-01 adjusted annually by CPI-U (Commissioner sets by Oct 1, 2028 and annually; adjustment not below zero). Trainees in on-the-job programme up to 90 days: greater of federal minimum or 75% of state rate (12.77 x 0.75 = 9.5775 -> 9.58 USD/h 2026, derived; rounding not stated in statute). History: 2020 cc.1204,1242; 2026 cc.350,351.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-28.9 Definitions; tipped employee (three dated versions)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum-wage 'employee' excludes (version until 2027-01-01): farm laborers; volunteers; golf caddies; commission outside salesmen, taxi drivers; under-18 employed by parent; inmates; summer-camp staff; under-16; students in bona fide educational programme; under-18 full-time students working <=20 h/week; full-time work-study students; babysitters <10 h/week; au pairs; H-2 temporary foreign workers (20 CFR 655); FLSA 213(a)(3) exempt. From 2027-01-01 (2026 cc.357,358) the farm-laborer exclusion is removed. Tipped employee = customarily receives > 30 USD/month in tips; tip credit = amount determined by employer (rebuttable by clear and convincing evidence); cannot classify as tipped where soliciting tips is prohibited. Wages include reasonable cost of customarily furnished meals and lodging.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-29 Time and medium of payment; withholding wages; written statement of earnings
figure_or_rule_carried: (B) regular pay periods: salaried at least monthly; hourly at least every two weeks or twice a month; monthly allowed for work-study students and, by agreement, employees whose weekly wages exceed 150% of the Commonwealth average weekly wage (65.2-500); on termination all wages paid on or before the next regular payday. (C) payment in cash, check, direct deposit to employee-designated account, or paycard with full fee disclosure and affirmative consent (paycard without consent only for hires after 2010-01-01 who do not designate an account, with one free withdrawal per pay period). (D) no deduction except taxes/law without written signed authorization; on each regular pay date a written statement by paystub or online accounting: employer name and address; hours worked (hourly, or salaried below the FLSA 13(a)(1) salary level); rate of pay; gross wages; amount and purpose of each deduction; sufficient to compute gross and net; keep 3 years from the work; agricultural employers only on request. (H) liquidated damages equal amount + 8% interest; (K) treble damages if knowing; (P, from 2026-07-01, 2026 c.1040) good-faith defense if cured within 14 days.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-29.2 Overtime: employer liability
figure_or_rule_carried: No separate state overtime standard: an employer violating FLSA overtime requirements is liable under 40.1-29(K); FLSA definitions, exemptions and overtime calculation methods apply; 3-year limitation. Result: overtime = FLSA 1.5x over 40 h/week, no daily overtime.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-33.3 Paid sick leave - definitions (home health workers)
figure_or_rule_carried: Paid sick leave article covers only 'home health workers' (consumer-directed personal care, respite or companion services under the state Medicaid plan) working on average >= 20 h/week or 90 h/month; paid at the normal hourly rate with same benefits, not below the 40.1-28.10 minimum wage without tip credit. instrument_name: Va. Code 63.2-1946 Employers to report new hires and new independent contractors

figure_or_rule_carried: Report each newly hired employee within 20 days of employment (as defined in 60.2-212) and each new independent contractor within 20 days of contract start; content = 42 USC 653a items only; by copy of W-4/W-9, electronic transmission in prescribed format or other means; electronic reporters: two monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart; multistate employers may designate one state with notice to HHS and copy to the Center.

instrument_name: Va. Code 34-29 Maximum portion of disposable earnings subject to garnishment (two dated versions)
figure_or_rule_carried: Ordinary garnishment: lesser of 25% of weekly disposable earnings or the excess over 40 x the greater of the federal or Virginia minimum hourly wage (2026: 40 x 12.77 = 510.80 USD/week protected, derived) - stricter than CCPA 30x. Support orders: 50% (supporting another spouse/child) / 60%, 55%/65% if arrears > 12 weeks. Limits do not apply to support orders, Chapter XIII bankruptcy, and (version until 2027-07-01) state or federal tax debts; version from 2027-07-01 (2026 c.396) lists only federal tax debts. No discharge for garnishment for any one indebtedness. Other pay periods: multiple set by Commissioner of Labor regulation.

instrument_name: VEC FAQs - Employer UI tax (liability, rates, wage base, quarterly report, Web Upload, separation report)
article_or_section: Employer Profile; Tax rates; Filing; Web Upload Filing; Reimbursable vs Contributory
figure_or_rule_carried: Liability: liable for FUTA, or quarterly payroll >= 1,500 USD, or an employee in 20 weeks in a calendar year; domestic employers when cash wages for domestic service >= 1,000 USD in a calendar quarter (annual filing option via ESS if quarterly payroll history < 5,000 USD, approval in advance); 501(c)(3) with < 4 employees in 20 weeks exempt. Localization: report where services are localized, else direction-and-control base. Base rates 0.1%-6.2%; new employer 2.5% plus add-ons; assigned 6.2% for no taxable payroll in 4 fiscal years, out-of-state construction contractors (3 years), delinquent employers; experience rate = benefit ratio over up to 4 fiscal years to June 30 applied to the Trust Fund balance factor; add-ons: pool cost charge (all employers, % not on page) and fund building charge 0.2% when trust fund balance <= 50%. Taxable wage base first 8,000 USD per employee per year (worked excess-wage example). UI gross wages = after section 125 deductions, before 401(k)/IRA-SEP/403(b) deductions; imputed group-term life over 50,000 USD differs from Medicare. Quarterly report due last day of the month after quarter end (Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31), next business day if weekend/holiday, via ESS, eForm or Web Upload; late report penalty 100 USD per report (not for quarters with no wages); paper only with waiver. Web Upload file types: Excel, column-based MMREF/EFW2 and ICESA, delimited; amendments on paper FC-34 (or wagereconciliation@ for > 4 records). Separation: VEC sends Report of Separation and Wage Information to the last 30-day/240-hour employer via SIDES/ESS when a claim is filed. Page readable by curl 2026-11-02 (previously 403).

authority: Virginia General Assembly (Code of Virginia); Virginia Employment Commission

No contribution in 2026 or 2027.

instrument_name: Va. Code 40.1-33.6:1 to 40.1-33.6:7 Paid Sick Leave (Article 2.1:1), effective July 1, 2027
authority: Virginia General Assembly (Code of Virginia); DOLI Commissioner
figure_or_rule_carried: ENACTED, NOT YET IN FORCE (operating level: employer payroll/leave accrual). Covered employer phase-in: 50+ employees from 2027-07-01; 25+ from 2028-01-01; 1+ from 2029-01-01; includes the Commonwealth and political subdivisions; home health workers stay under 40.1-33.3. Accrual 1 hour per 30 hours worked from start of employment; carry-over; accrual and use capped at 40 hours per year (employer-defined 12-month year) unless employer sets higher; FLSA 13(a)(1)-exempt employees deemed 40 h/week (or normal shorter week); front-load of 40 hours satisfies accrual; PTO policy or CBA meeting the standard suffices; no payout on separation; reinstatement if rehired within 12 months unless paid out; successor employer carries balances; employer may advance leave. Paid at the regular rate as defined in 40.1-29.3(B), not below the 40.1-28.10 minimum without tip credit. Use: increments no greater than 4 hours; documentation only for 3+ consecutive work days. Commissioner regulations: written notice and posting, 3-year records of accrual and use, confidentiality. Longshore CBA exemption until CBA expiry or 2030-12-31.

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 481 Earned sick time definitions (covered employee)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employee = employed an average of at least 18 h/week during a year. Excluded: federal employees; jobs of 20 weeks or fewer in 12 months AND scheduled 20 weeks or fewer; exempt/excluded State classified service; per-diem/intermittent health-care facility staff; non-regular substitute educators; under 18 years of age; sole proprietors/partners and approved excluded executive officers/LLC members (WC exclusions 601(14)(F),(H)); per-diem/intermittent workers who work only when available with no obligation or expectation of continuing employment. Employer = any employer doing business or operating in the State (no headcount floor in this section).

instrument_name: 21 V.S.A. 483 Use of earned sick time (use cap; carry-over; no payout)
figure_or_rule_carried: Uses: own illness/care, family care, domestic violence services, closure of school/business. Increments: smallest the payroll system uses, not below 1 hour required. Use cap: employer may limit use to 40 h per 12 months. Unused time carries over (unless paid out at period end at the employer's discretion, which then does not carry over). No payment of unused earned sick time on separation unless the employer agrees. Rehire within 12 months after discharge: no new waiting period (prior balance not retained unless agreed). Hour-trading in the same pay period allowed.

instrument_name: 9 V.S.A. 2440 Social Security Number Protection Act

No pay-statement truncation rule as such: a mailed pay statement may not carry the full SSN (no law requires it there); a redacted SSN is outside the prohibition.

Final pay on quit or discharge: no later than the employer's usual regular payday (or CBA time); employer may offset sums the employee owes; commission sales agents with custody of accounts excluded; 18% p.a. interest plus attorney fees on suit (27-4-104). Wages include fringe benefits; accrued vacation is wages (payable at termination) unless a written forfeiture policy is acknowledged in writing by the employee (27-4-501(a)(iii)). DWS wage claims capped at 2 months' wages outside bankruptcy (27-4-502(a)). Tips are the employee's sole property (27-4-507(a)). Wage assignments for loans under 200 USD need written employer acceptance and filing; a married employee needs the spouse's written consent (27-4-110/111). instrument_name: W.S. 27-3-102(a)(xviii) definition of wage for UI contributions (taxable wage base and exclusions); 27-3-303(a) statewide average annual wage

Excluded from wage (to the extent not FUTA wages): retirement/sickness/medical/death plan premiums; employer-paid FICA; non-obligatory dismissal pay; tips not reportable under 3306(s); convenience meals/lodging on premises; sick pay after 6 months of illness; sec. 125 benefits excluding cash; wages of a deceased worker paid after the year of death; sec. 129 dependent care; educational assistance; achievement awards; sec. 120 legal services; group-term life cost; moving expenses; employer contributions to qualified plans/IRA and 403(b); SUB payments; workers' compensation benefits. 8% of the average annual wage rounded to the lowest 50 USD = monetary eligibility (27-3-306(d)(i)).

instrument_name: W.S. 27-3-105, 27-3-107, 27-3-108 UI coverage: government, nonprofit, religious, agricultural, domestic, excluded services
figure_or_rule_carried: Covered: state and political-subdivision service incl. appointed officials (105(a)(i)); 3306(c)(8) nonprofits with 4+ individuals in 20 weeks (a)(ii); Indian tribes (a)(iii). Agricultural labor covered at 20,000 USD cash wages in a quarter or 10+ workers in 20 weeks (107(c)); H-2A workers exempt while FUTA exempts them (107(h)). Domestic service covered at 1,000 USD cash wages in a quarter (107(g)). Excluded: service for a spouse or child, under-21 child for a parent (108(a)(i)); federal service; under-18 newspaper carriers/direct sellers; licensed real-estate agents; students employed by their school and spouses in financial-aid programmes; certified co-op students; hospital patients; booth-rent barbers/stylists; leased owner-operators with contract; casual labor (under 50 USD, outside the course of business); LLC members unless the LLC elects (108(a)(xiii)).
